'''K2 Black Panther''' ({{Korean|hangul=K-2 흑표|hanja=K-2 黑豹|rr=K-2 Heukpyo}}) is a South Korean [[List of main battle tanks by generation#Fourth Generation|fourth-generation]] [[main battle tank]] (MBT),  designed by the [[Agency for Defense Development]] and manufactured by [[Hyundai Rotem]]. The tank's design began in the 1990s to meet the strategic requirements of the [[Republic of Korea Army]]'s reform for [[Three-Dimensional (3D) Tactics Analysis|three-dimensional]], high-speed [[maneuver warfare]]<ref name="KBS 1997-10-01">{{cite web|url=https://news.kbs.co.kr/news/view.do?ncd=3766437|script-title=ko:입체 고속 기동전|publisher=[[Korean Broadcasting System|KBS]]|date=1 October 1996|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221211081707/https://news.kbs.co.kr/news/view.do?ncd=3766437|archive-date=11 December 2022|access-date=11 December 2022|author=}}</ref> based on use of [[network-centric warfare]].<ref name="JAKO200820549300606">{{cite web |author=Kim Seok and Son Seung-hyun |date=31 December 2008 |title=A Concept Study on Efficiently Improving Performance for Korean MBT |url=https://koreascience.kr/article/JAKO200820549300606.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230709060651/https://koreascience.kr/article/JAKO200820549300606.pdf |archive-date=9 July 2023 |access-date=9 July 2023 |publisher=Defense Agency for Technology and Quality}}</ref><ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 1">{{cite web |author=Defense Media Agency |date=10 March 2016 |title= |script-title=ko:[첨단국가의 초석, 방위산업] 세계수준의 명품, K2 흑표전차 ① |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DhSK5uL6sgE |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221211043314/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DhSK5uL6sgE |archive-date=11 December 2022 |access-date=11 December 2022 |publisher=국방}}</ref><ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 2">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4XB52Xx5RoI|script-title=ko:[첨단국가의 초석, 방위산업] 세계수준의 명품, K2 흑표전차 ②|publisher=국방TV|date=5 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221211043250/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4XB52Xx5RoI|archive-date=11 December 2022|access-date=11 December 2022|author=Defense Media Agency}}</ref>

Over its predecessor, the [[K1 tank|K1]], the K2 features improved protection, mobility, firepower, increased indigenous production, and crew operability. The focus of the design places emphasis on lower weight, higher mobility and increased [[modularity]]. The K2 Black Panther also acquired several modern features such as extensive integration of [[Vetronics]], advanced sensors, space optimization, and increased automation.<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 1" /><ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 2" />

Development of the K2 entered System Concept Research phase in 1995, Exploratory development from 1998 to 2002, and started Full Scale Development in June 2003. Development of the vehicle excluding the [[Powerpack (drivetrain)|powerpack]] concluded in 2008, following trials by the army. Work on the domestic powerpack kept the tanks from entering service until in 2012, when 100 [[EuroPowerPack]]s were implemented on the first production batch. The first 6 K2 Black Panthers entered service with the [[Republic of Korea Army]] on June 29, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-05-30 |title=K2 흑표전차 내달 15대 실전배치…그 위력은 |url=https://www.khan.co.kr/article/201405301913141 |access-date=2026-03-03 |website=Default |language=ko|publication-place=Republic of Korea}}</ref><ref name="YTN 2014-09-27">{{cite web|url=https://www.ytn.co.kr/_ln/0101_201409271628248651|title=K2전차 실전배치후 첫 공개...'백발백중'|publisher=[[YTN]]|date=27 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230918035428/https://www.ytn.co.kr/_ln/0101_201409271628248651|archive-date=18 September 2023|access-date=18 September 2023|author=Kim Moon-kyung}}</ref>

== History ==
=== Development ===
South Korea has been accumulating tank development and production technology to increase its self-reliance in producing arms. In 1976, South Korea upgraded its [[M48 Patton]] tanks. In 1987, the [[K1 tank|K1 88-Tank]], designed by [[General Dynamics Land Systems]] (GDLS), was commissioned for service. South Korea participated in its development, and gained tank production and partial development capabilities. The K1 was a derivative of the [[M1 Abrams]], designed by Americans and produced in South Korea, and its associated legal agreements limited South Korea's rights for [[Arms exports|export]], [[logistics]], and future enhancements.<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 1" /><ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 2" /><ref name="K1 Developers Interview Part 1">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ucDjQtMbuas|script-title=ko:[첨단국가의 초석, 방위산업] 한국형 전차 K1 개발사 ①|publisher=국방TV|date=17 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221211071147/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ucDjQtMbuas|archive-date=11 December 2022|access-date=11 December 2022|author=Defense Media Agency}}</ref><ref name="K1A1 Developers Interview">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FBSvXJL2eW0|script-title=ko:[첨단국가의 초석, 방위산업] 한국형 전차 K1A1|publisher=국방TV|date=10 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221211071406/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FBSvXJL2eW0|archive-date=11 December 2022|access-date=11 December 2022|author=Defense Media Agency}}</ref>

In the early 1990s, Korean engineers suggested producing a new domestically designed tank using the latest available technology, but the military refused due to cost overruns. Instead, South Korea chose to upgrade the K1, and received a technical data upgrade package from GDLS. However, it was limiting its involvement to strengthen its [[Defense industrial base]] while taking responsibility for possible failure. South Korea advanced in turret designs, [[fire-control system|fire-control systems]], sights, and [[Composite armour|composite armor]] during this process. The operational prototype of the new variant [[K1 88-Tank#K1A1|K1A1]] was later displayed in 1996, but the [[1997 Asian financial crisis]] delayed its [[mass production]]. South Korea worked on further localization during the delay and managed to develop its own designs or produce most parts of the K1A1 under license.<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 2"/><ref name="K1A1 Developers Interview"/>

While K1A1 development was ongoing, South Korea began to plan a new domestic main battle tank as its tank design and manufacturing capability matured. There were three main reasons for the development of the new tank:

Firstly, despite the increase in localization, K1A1 was still an American design that falls under the United States' [[export control]] to protect [[Intellectual property|intellectual rights]], which creates a burden when exporting.

Secondly, the M48A3K and the M48A5K operated by the [[Republic of Korea Armed Forces|South Korean military]] were aging designs and needed to be replaced with newer, improved designs.<ref name="Bemil 20211015">{{cite web|url=https://bemil.chosun.com/site/data/html_dir/2021/10/01/2021100101693.html|title=K2 흑표 전차|publisher=bemil|date=15 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220930100530/https://bemil.chosun.com/site/data/html_dir/2021/10/01/2021100101693.html|archive-date=30 September 2022|access-date=18 August 2022|author=Yoon Sang-yong}}</ref><ref name="Security Fact 20180625">{{cite web|url=http://www.securityfact.co.kr/news/view.php?no=725|script-title=ko:[한국무기 디테일] ⑫ 국내 국방과학기술이 총 결집된 현대 로템의 K2 흑표 전차|publisher=Security Fact|date=25 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220930083444/http://www.securityfact.co.kr/news/view.php?no=725|archive-date=30 September 2022|access-date=30 September 2022|author=Kim Han-gyeong}}</ref>

Thirdly, the [[Republic of Korea Army]] was adapting new tactics called [[Three-Dimensional (3D) Tactics Analysis|three-dimensional]] high-speed [[maneuver warfare]] with [[network-centric warfare]].<ref name="KBS 1997-10-01" /><ref name="JAKO200820549300606" /> When developers asked the Army what kind of performance the Army wanted to see with the new tank, the Army replied that network warfare capability for [[command and control]] is the top priority, not [[firepower]], defense, or [[Mobility (military)|mobility]]. This new capability would need to be built into the new tank.<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 1"/><ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 2"/>

Criticism was made on the new tank developments: "It seemed to many to be too early to adopt a new model, and there were also doubts because it would be the first tank ever designed domestically." However, consensus of the defense sector (the politicians, the military, and developers) viewed the K1 tanks as a "humiliation", because the tank itself was a proof that South Korea lacked in tank developing technology. It was a matter of national pride to have the ability to design and build a leading main battle tank.<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 2"/>

Developers claimed that during times of war, [[military logistics]] and [[Combat service support|support]] of armaments could stop when geopolitics came into play, as witnessed in the [[Middle East]] and [[Eastern Europe]]. There were also criticisms of many European nations as lacking investment in domestic warfare technology, and relying too much on weapons from [[partnership]]s. Historically, South Korea always maintained a policy of self-reliance on weapons, and so the new tank program was authorized.<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 2"/>

From July 1995 to December 1997, system concept research was conducted including analysis of required operational capability (ROC), function, performance, operations, logistics, and the technology required. The first step was to develop a modeling and simulation system for theoretical study and analysis. South Korean developers invited experts from around the world, including [[Sven Berge]] ([[Stridsvagn 103]]), [[Philip Lett]] ([[M1 Abrams]]), [[Israel Tal]] ([[Merkava]]), Hayashi Iwao ([[Type 90 tank|Type 90]]), and [[Richard Ogorkiewicz]] (European tanks) for a 40-hour seminar to help guide the concepts of the new tank development. Per prior agreement, all the presentations were recorded, and used for guiding system development of the new tank. Then seven researchers of the [[Agency for Defense Development]] (ADD), who were responsible for designing the tank, were sent to the [[United Kingdom]] for a year of tank development education.<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 2"/><ref name="Security Fact 20180625"/><ref name="XT2-2006-0878">{{cite web|url=https://www.ntis.go.kr/outcomes/tpopup/xtApplDtlInfoAction.do?cmd=best&techId=XT2-2006-0878&returnURI=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubnRpcy5nby5rci9UaFNlYXJjaFRvdGFsTGlzdC5kbz9zb3J0PVJBTkslMkZERVNDJm50aXNZbj0mc2VhcmNoV29yZD0lRUMlQTAlODQlRUMlQjAlQTgmb3JpZ2luYWxTZWFyY2hXb3JkPSZvcmlnaW5hbFNlYXJjaEd1YnVuPQ%3D%3D&pageCode=TH_TOTAL_BEST_RST_DTL|script-title=ko:세계 11번째 독자 개발된 차기전차|publisher=National Science & Technology Information Service|date=2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220413024017/https://www.ntis.go.kr/outcomes/tpopup/xtApplDtlInfoAction.do?cmd=best&techId=XT2-2006-0878&returnURI=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubnRpcy5nby5rci9UaFNlYXJjaFRvdGFsTGlzdC5kbz9zb3J0PVJBTkslMkZERVNDJm50aXNZbj0mc2VhcmNoV29yZD0lRUMlQTAlODQlRUMlQjAlQTgmb3JpZ2luYWxTZWFyY2hXb3JkPSZvcmlnaW5hbFNlYXJjaEd1YnVuPQ%3D%3D&pageCode=TH_TOTAL_BEST_RST_DTL|archive-date=13 April 2022|access-date=13 April 2022|author=Kim Ui-hwan}}</ref>

From November 1998 to December 2002, private companies joined the ADD during [[exploratory research]], and developed core technologies and systems including the [[tank gun]], the electric gun and turret drive system (EGTDS), and the gun [[autoloader]]. Other key systems and tests included automatic target detection & tracking, and cognitive identification ability of the combat control system along with its simulator, the [[Active suspension#Adaptive and semi-active|semi-active in-arm suspension]] unit to dramatically increase mobility performance, and the [[Proximity fuze|proximity fuse]] (within 7 meters) for multi-purpose [[High-explosive anti-tank|HEAT]] munition (to shoot down helicopters).<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 2"/><ref name="XT2-2006-0878" /><ref name="Hyundai Rotem 20170921">{{cite web|url=https://blog.hyundai-rotem.co.kr/44|script-title=ko:승리의 검은 표범! 현대로템 K2전차 '흑표' 지식테스트|publisher=[[Hyundai Rotem]]|date=21 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210708105713/https://blog.hyundai-rotem.co.kr/44|archive-date=8 July 2021|access-date=8 July 2021|author=}}</ref>

[[File:육군 K2전차 (7445555272).jpg|thumb|XK2 PV3 firing its cannon]]

In 2002, [[Hilmi Özkök]], the commander of [[Turkish Land Forces]], visited the research center and witnessed the simulator capabilities and an actual model of the combat control system. Afterward, Turkey continuously sent its dignitaries to closely monitor progress, and it eventually led to cooperation in developing Turkey's [[Altay (main battle tank)|Altay]].<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 2"/>

From January 2003 to 2007, a number of test vehicles were built:  two test vehicles, the MTR (Mobility Test Rig) and FTR (Firepower Test Rig), and three PV (Pilot Vehicles) were built to demonstrate technology and performance. MTR and FTR conducted mobility, fire control, combat control, and low temperature operating life tests, while PV1, PV2, and PV3 conducted tests on endurance, developer, operator, and [[integrated logistics support]].<ref name="Security Fact 20180625"/> The last prototype was unveiled on 2 March 2007 at the [[proving ground]] in [[Changwon]],<ref name="Hyundai Rotem 20170921" /><ref name="SBS 20070302">{{cite web|url=https://news.sbs.co.kr/news/endPage.do?news_id=N1000226213|script-title=ko:강바닥 달리는 국산 '차기전차(XK2)' 개발|publisher=[[Seoul Broadcasting System|SBS]]|date=2 March 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220818183928/https://news.sbs.co.kr/news/endPage.do?news_id=N1000226213|archive-date=18 August 2022|access-date=18 August 2022|author=}}</ref> and the development was officially completed after being declared fit for combat by the [[Defense Acquisition Program Administration]] (DAPA) in September 2008. The XK2 development project, which began in 1995 and ended in 2008, cost a total of 452.6 billion [[South Korean won|won]] spread over 14 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kistep.re.kr/boardDownload.es?bid=0031&list_no=42886&seq=1|title=[KISTEP 브리프] K-방산 수출 성과와 민군 R&D 협력의 주요 시사점|publisher=Korea Institute of Science & Technology Evaluation and Planning|date=16 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221007190414/https://www.kistep.re.kr/boardDownload.es?bid=0031&list_no=42886&seq=1|archive-date=7 October 2022|access-date=7 October 2022|author=Investment Planning and Coordination Center}} p. 4</ref>

=== Improvement ===
In 2020, [[Samyang Comtech]], which produces composite armors, began developing an improvement of front armors for K2 export variants,<ref name="Samyang Comtech Accomplishments">{{cite web|url=https://samyangct.com/eng/performance-progress/|title=Development Performance & Progress|publisher=[[Samyang Comtech]]|date=|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260815233735/https://samyangct.com/eng/performance-progress/|archivedate=15 August 2026|accessdate=15 August 2026|author1=}}</ref> and later it changed to a modification and development project to completely improve the modular armor for export variants organized by the Defense Agency for Technology and Quality (DTaQ) in 2021.<ref name="Samyang Comtech History">{{cite web|url=https://samyangct.com/eng/history/|title=History|publisher=[[Samyang Comtech]]|date=|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260815212451/https://samyangct.com/eng/history/|archivedate=15 August 2026|accessdate=15 August 2026|author1=}}</ref>

The third mass-produced K2, which began in 2022, included an improved [[Battlefield management system|Battlefield Management System]] with the Korean Variable Message Format (KVMF),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://koreascience.kr/article/JAKO201406234294852.pdf|title=An Implementation of KVMF(Korean Variable Message Format) in the Battlefield Management System of Ground Fighting Vehicles|publisher=[[LIG Nex1]]|date=5 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230205145643/https://koreascience.kr/article/JAKO201406234294852.pdf|archive-date=5 February 2023|access-date=5 February 2023|author=Choi Il-ho}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://koreascience.kr/article/JAKO202010163249969.pdf|title=An Implementation of Target Information Management and its Sharing Process among Ground Fighting Vehicles|publisher=[[LIG Nex1]]|date=5 February == Design ==
=== Weapon system and munitions ===
[[File:2014 대한민국 방위산업전(DX Korea) 육군의 명품 무기와 장비 소개 (15393852929).jpg|thumb|A K2 tank on display along with its K280 [[High-explosive anti-tank|HEAT-MP-T]] munition rounds and K6 heavy machine gun rounds]]

The main gun and its munitions were developed simultaneously. In the early to mid 1990s, South Korea learned [[internal ballistics]], [[external ballistics]], and [[terminal ballistics]] for tank guns while license producing the [[M256 (tank gun)|KM256 tank gun]]; they invented [[K1 88-Tank#Firepower|self-sharpening tungsten penetrator]] for 120&nbsp;mm [[Armour-piercing fin-stabilized discarding sabot|APFSDS]] munitions during the K1A1 program. Using acquired technology, engineers decided to increase firepower with longer gun barrels and enhanced propellants that were [[120×570mm NATO|NATO compatible]].<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 1"/><ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 3"/>

Compared to the {{convert|5.3|m|ft|sp=us}} long 44 caliber KM256, the new gun was {{convert|6.6|m|ft|sp=us}} in length and sent out projectiles at {{convert|12|-|13|MJ|kWh|sp=us}}, which was a huge increase from {{convert|8|-|9|MJ|kWh|sp=us}}. Since the projectile travels at [[hypersonic speed]] or at a muzzle velocity of 1,760&nbsp;m/s (with K279), it was critical to develop HEAT resistance material and stabilization of the projectile.<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 1"/><ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 3">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-KQ2tfaBAoU|script-title=ko:[첨단국가의 초석, 방위산업] 세계수준의 명품, K2 흑표전차 ③|publisher=국방TV|date=5 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221214115117/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-KQ2tfaBAoU|archive-date=14 December 2022|access-date=14 December 2022|author=Defense Media Agency}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://tv.dema.mil.kr/web/tv/replay/tvNewView.do?media_seq=800653|script-title=ko:지상전의 왕자 K1A1전차|publisher=Defense Media Agency|date=21 July 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220921052856/https://tv.dema.mil.kr/web/tv/replay/tvNewView.do?media_seq=800653|archive-date=21 September 2022|access-date=21 September 2022|author=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.add.re.kr/board?menuId=MENU02999&siteId=null|title=R&D Achievement 50|publisher=[[Agency for Defense Development]]|date=|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240314105708/https://www.add.re.kr/board?menuId=MENU02999&siteId=null|archivedate=14 March 2024|accessdate=14 March 2024|author1=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://dl.nanet.go.kr/file/fileDownload.do?linkSystemId=NADL&controlNo=NONB1201818281|script-title=ko:화기별·탄종별 사격장 안전기준 정립 연구|publisher=Republic of Korea Army Headquarters|date=25 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211014062442/https://dl.nanet.go.kr/file/fileDownload.do?linkSystemId=NADL&controlNo=NONB1201818281|archive-date=14 October 2021|access-date=14 October 2021|author=Security Management Institute}} p. 118</ref> Early designs included an unmanned turret variant, which was scrapped in favor of a manned turret during initial exploratory development. Another plan was to equip [[Rheinmetall]]'s experimental [[:de:Rheinmetall Neue Panzerkanone 140|NPzK-140]] 140&nbsp;mm smoothbore gun, but this plan was also scrapped due to issues regarding [[Combustion#Incomplete|incomplete combustion]] of 140&nbsp;mm munitions.<ref name="Chosun 20090410">{{cite web|url=http://monthly.chosun.com/client/news/viw.asp?nNewsNumb=200904100030|script-title=ko:조향 핸들 돌리자 55t의 전차가 사뿐하게 360도 자동회전|publisher=[[The Chosun Ilbo]]|date=10 April 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221001211818/http://monthly.chosun.com/client/news/viw.asp?nNewsNumb=200904100030|archive-date=1 October 2022|access-date=1 October 2022|author=Oh Dong-ryong}}</ref>

South Korea originally planned to receive technology transfer of [[Chrome plating#Arms use|chrome plating]] on tank guns from [[Switzerland]], only a handful of nations having such technology. However, the plan was changed to domestic development after hearing the refusal from Swiss firm. Engineers first tried chrome plating on the KM256 tank gun used by K1A1, then coincidentally found a classified method while reworking on defect-plated guns.<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 2"/>

The Black Panther is armed with a chrome plated [[CN08 120 mm gun|CN08 120 mm 55 caliber smoothbore gun]] developed by the ADD and WIA (now [[Hyundai WIA]]), and is capable of hitting a {{convert|30|cm|in|sp=us}} size object at range greater than {{convert|1|km|mi|sp=us}}.<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 1"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://file.mt.co.kr/newfiledown.php?filepath=2016%2F01&filen=I_Machinery_20160105_SK_1823257457_102350.pdf|script-title=ko:방위산업, 저성장 시대의 대안|publisher=SK Securities|date=5 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211028082233/https://file.mt.co.kr/newfiledown.php?filepath=2016%2F01&filen=I_Machinery_20160105_SK_1823257457_102350.pdf|archive-date=28 October 2021|access-date=28 October 2021|author=Lee Ji-hun}} p. 14</ref><ref name="Meta-Defense.fr">{{cite web|url=https://www.meta-defense.fr/en/2021/09/15/altay-black-panther-oplot-what-modern-battle-tanks-are-worth-3-3/|title=Altay, Black Panther, Oplot: What are modern battle tanks worth? 3/3|publisher=Meta-Defense.fr|date=15 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220417005727/https://www.meta-defense.fr/en/2021/09/15/altay-black-panther-oplot-what-modern-battle-tanks-are-worth-3-3/|archive-date=17 April 2022|access-date=17 April 2022|author=}}</ref> This is complemented by a home-grown bustle-type autoloader, similar to the [[Leclerc tank|Leclerc]], which allows the tank to fire up to 10 rounds per minute.<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 2"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.donga.com/news/Politics/article/all/20150206/69506413/1|script-title=ko:파워팩 논란 K2전차 "전력화 이상무"... 1.2km 떨어진 1.2m 표적지에 '쾅쾅'|publisher=[[The Dong-A Ilbo]]|date=6 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221003185739/https://www.donga.com/news/Politics/article/all/20150206/69506413/1|archive-date=3 October 2022|access-date=3 October 2022|author=Jung Seong-taek}}</ref><ref name="sciencetimes-140519">{{cite web|url=https://www.sciencetimes.co.kr/news/%EB%AF%B8%EB%9E%98%EC%9D%98-%EC%A0%84%EC%B0%A8%EB%8A%94-%EB%A9%88%EC%B6%94%EB%A9%B4-%EC%82%B4-%EC%88%98-%EC%97%86%EB%8B%A4/|script-title=ko:미래의 전차는 멈추면 살 수 없다|publisher=The Science Times|date=19 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210708090521/https://www.sciencetimes.co.kr/news/%EB%AF%B8%EB%9E%98%EC%9D%98-%EC%A0%84%EC%B0%A8%EB%8A%94-%EB%A9%88%EC%B6%94%EB%A9%B4-%EC%82%B4-%EC%88%98-%EC%97%86%EB%8B%A4/|archive-date=8 July 2021|access-date=8 July 2021|author=Jo Haeng-man}}</ref> The laser [[barcode]] identifier of the autoloader recognizes the classification of pre-barcoded ammunition and selects a type of munition for loading based on mission need. The ammunition is loaded in a 16-shell magazine for ready-to-use, and 24 rounds at frontal hull, carrying a total of 40 rounds for its main armament.<ref name="sciencetimes-140519" />

The K2's primary anti-tank munitions, developed by the ADD and [[Poongsan Corporation]], are the [[CN08 120 mm gun#Ammunition|K279 APFSDS-T]], designed with self-sharpening technology for armored targets, and the  [[CN08 120 mm gun#Ammunition|K280 HEAT-MP-T]], a multipurpose chemical energy round with a proximity fuse that explodes within 7 meters from the target, for all types of targets including low-flying helicopters.<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 2"/>

Secondary weapons include a 12.7&nbsp;mm [[M2 Browning|K6 Heavy Machine Gun]]  and a 7.62&nbsp;mm M60E2-1 coaxial machine gun. The trigger pull of the coaxial machine gun lightened from {{convert|4|kg|lb|sp=us}} to {{convert|3|kg|lb|sp=us}} for convenience.<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 1"/>

==== Korean Smart Top-Attack Munition (KSTAM) ====
{{Main|KSTAM}}

The Korean Smart Top-Attack Munition (KSTAM) was a research project to develop a [[fire-and-forget]], top-attack anti-tank munition with an effective operating range of {{convert|2–8|km|mi|sp=us}}. It was developed specifically for use with the K2. Two different concepts were investigated: The KSTAM-I concept developed jointly by Hanwha and [[Israeli Military Industries]] and the KSTAM-II concept developed by Doosan in cooperation with [[Diehl Defence]] of Germany.<ref name="KSTAM1" /> 

The KSTAM-I projectile had a tandem shaped charge warhead, folding canards and a small rocket motor.<ref name="KSTAM1" /> The projectile would detect the target using its own seeker and then hit the roof in a pitch-down trajectory similar to that of other [[top-attack]] anti-tank guided missiles (ATGMs).

Meanwhile, the KSTAM-II's projectile housed a scaled-down version of Diehl's [[SMArt 155]] sub-munition. Upon reaching its designated target area, the projectile would eject the sub-munition. A parachute would then deploy, giving the sub-munitions on-board [[Extremely high frequency|millimeter band]] [[radar]], [[infrared]] and [[radiometer]] sensors time to seek and acquire stationary or moving targets.<ref name="KSTAM1"/><ref name="KSTAM2"/>

Once a target has been acquired, the [[explosively formed penetrator]] (EFP) warhead is fired from a top-down position, to exploit the weaker top armor of tanks. Target acquisition can also be directed manually by the tank crew via a remote link. These characteristics allow the launch vehicle to remain concealed behind cover while firing successive rounds towards the known location of an enemy, or provide [[indirect fire]] support against targets hidden behind obstacles and structures.<ref name="KSTAM1">{{cite web|url=https://www.koreascience.or.kr/article/JAKO200626055835151.pdf|title=A Trade Study of the Top Attack Smart Tank Ammunition|publisher=Journal of the Korea Society of Systems Engineering|date=31 January 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211017052608/https://www.koreascience.or.kr/article/JAKO200626055835151.pdf|archive-date=17 October 2021|access-date=17 October 2021|author=[[Agency for Defense Development]]}}</ref><ref name="KSTAM2">{{cite web|url=http://journal.kadis.or.kr/UPFILE/PUBLICATION_FILE/J2016048/160104.pdf|title=Systems Analysis on Smart Ammunition for 120mm Tank Gun|publisher=Korea Association of Defense Industry Studies|date=June 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220330053548/http://journal.kadis.or.kr/UPFILE/PUBLICATION_FILE/J2016048/160104.pdf|archive-date=30 March 2022|access-date=30 March 2022|author=Poongsan Technology Institute}}</ref>

The Korean Smart Top-Attack Munition (KSTAM) remained a research topic and neither the KSTAM-I nor the KSTAM-II reached series readiness.

=== Fire-control system and optics ===

The fire-control system (FCS) consists gunner's primary sight (GPS), commander's panoramic sight (CPS), [[Ballistics|ballistic]] calculator, electrical gun and turret drive system (EGTDS), and dynamic [[muzzle reference system]] (DMRS).<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 1"/>

The K2 is equipped with an advanced fire-control system linked to an [[Extremely high frequency|Extremely High Frequency]] (EHF) [[L band (NATO)|L-band]] [[Pulse-Doppler radar|Pulsed Doppler Radar]] system deployed on the frontal arc of the turret,<ref name="JAKO200925265919312">{{cite web|url=https://koreascience.kr/article/JAKO200925265919312.pdf|title=L-band Pulsed Doppler Radar Development for Main Battle Tank|publisher=[[Agency for Defense Development]]|date=30 June 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220806190902/https://koreascience.kr/article/JAKO200925265919312.pdf|archive-date=6 August 2022|access-date=6 August 2022|author1=Gyu-Churl Park|author2=Jong-Soo Ha}}</ref> along with a VAS-1K [[raman laser]] [[rangefinder]] and crosswind sensor. The system is capable of a "lock-on" mode, which can acquire and track specific targets up to a range of {{convert|9.8|km|mi|sp=us}} using a [[thermographic camera]].<ref name="SBS 20070302" /><ref name="Chosun 20090410" /><ref name="KGPS">{{cite web|url=https://www.edaily.co.kr/news/read?newsId=01108646612619072&mediaCodeNo=257|title=[e-무기]미국산 불량품 고치다 탄생한 한국형 전차의 '눈'|publisher=[[Edaily]]|date=23 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220522172622/https://www.edaily.co.kr/news/read?newsId=01108646612619072&mediaCodeNo=257|archive-date=22 May 2022|access-date=22 May 2022|author=Kim Gwan-yong}}</ref> This allows the crew to fire accurately while moving as well as engage low-flying aircraft.

The fire-control system is also linked to an advanced gun stabilizer and trigger-delay mechanism to optimize accuracy while moving in uneven terrain. If the trigger on the main gun is pulled at the same time the tank encounters an irregularity in the terrain, oscillation of the gun barrel will cause temporary misalignment between a mirror-type laser reflector at the top of the barrel and a laser emitter (vertical sensor unit) at the base. This will delay the fire-control system from activating until the beam is re-aligned, improving the chances of hitting the intended target.<ref name="sciencetimes-140519" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.koreascience.or.kr/article/JAKO201613752757718.pdf|title=A Study on Measurement of Gun's Attitude of K2 MBT Using Inertial Navigation System and Its Effects on the Hit Probability|publisher=[[Hyundai Rotem]]|date=5 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210707055320/https://www.koreascience.or.kr/article/JAKO201613752757718.pdf|archive-date=7 July 2021|access-date=7 July 2021|author=Sungho Kim}}</ref>

The Korean Commander's Panoramic Sight (KCPS) and the Korean Gunner's Primary Sight (KGPS) are present in the Black Panther as in the original series of [[K1 88-Tank#Electronics and sensors|K1A1]] tanks, albeit redesigned to utilize the more advanced sensors and armaments deployed on the K2.<ref name="Chosun 20090410" /><ref name="KGPS" /> The K2's Korean Gunner's Primary Sight adopts a thermographic camera that is more advanced than K1A1, and the sight provides 4x and 15x magnifications using the [[optical]] system, and 30x and 60x magnifications using a [[Digital image processing|digital image processor]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://koreascience.kr/article/JAKO200502637471715.pdf|title=Advanced LWIR Thermal Imaging Sight Design|publisher=[[Agency for Defense Development]]|date=1 June 2005|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221004171006/https://koreascience.kr/article/JAKO200502637471715.pdf|archive-date=4 October 2022|access-date=4 October 2022|author=Hong Seok-min, Kim Hyun-sook and Park Yong-chan}}</ref>

The [[tank gun]] and [[Gun turret|turret]] are powered by an EGTDS developed by [[Hyundai Rotem]] and Doosan Mottrol (now [[Mottrol]]). The EGTDS provides high efficiency and high precision drive control, and its performance is improved by 3-axis stabilization. It is also designed to minimize vibration and noise when the turret is driven.<ref name="Hyundai Rotem 20170921" /><ref name="Mottrol">{{cite web|url=https://www.mottrol.com/download/defense/MOTTROL_Defense_Catalogue.pdf|title=Defense Applications & Solutions|publisher=[[Mottrol]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221230075312/https://www.mottrol.com/download/defense/MOTTROL_Defense_Catalogue.pdf|archive-date=30 December 2022|access-date=30 December 2022|author=}} p. 5</ref> The turret achieved a rotating speed of 800&nbsp;mil (45 degrees) per second at the prototype stage.<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 2"/>

The commander of the tank has the ability to override the gunner's command, to take control of the turret and gun. Moreover, unconfirmed reports state that, in the event of an emergency, the vehicle can be operated by only two crew members, or even a single one. It is speculated that the fire-control system can automatically spot and track visible targets, compare them using the data link established with other friendly vehicles to prevent redundant target engagements, and fire its main gun without manual input.

==== Automatic Target Detection and Tracking System ====
K2 has an Automatic Target Detection and Tracking System controlled by the [[Automatic target recognition|Automatic Target Recognition]] algorithm.<ref name="JAKO200734516358474">{{cite web|url=https://koreascience.kr/article/JAKO200734516358474.pdf|title=A ballistic lead-computation method to improve firing accuracy of army combat vehicles|publisher=[[Agency for Defense Development]]|date=29 June 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230128070857/https://koreascience.kr/article/JAKO200734516358474.pdf|archive-date=28 January 2023|access-date=28 January 2023|author=Jeoun, Young-Mi}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|url=http://audio.dn.naver.com/audio/ncr/1406_1/20120817134910420_IXSJJILJ4.pdf|script-title=ko:지상군의 핵심전력 전차에 관한 고찰|publisher=Journal of Military History Studies|date=January 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200331134532/http://audio.dn.naver.com/audio/ncr/1406_1/20120817134910420_IXSJJILJ4.pdf|issn=2093-1557|pages=322–349|archive-date=31 March 2020|access-date=31 March 2020|author=Kim Jang-heum|journal=Kunsa Yŏn'gu }}</ref><ref name="ADD 1">{{cite web|url=https://www.add.re.kr/board?menuId=MENU02834&siteId=SITE00003|title=K2 Tank|publisher=[[Agency for Defense Development]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220801183850/https://www.add.re.kr/board?menuId=MENU02834&siteId=SITE00003|archive-date=1 August 2022|access-date=1 August 2022|author=}}</ref> When the target is identified as a foe by the [[Identification friend or foe|IFF/SIF]] (Identification Friend or Foe/Selective Identification Feature) system, the tank automatically aims and performs laser distance measurements on the target even if the tank is maneuvering on irregular terrain while the target is moving. It can [[Deflection (ballistics)|lead the target]] and fire automatically based on ballistic data calculated by the turret mounted laser rangefinder and crosswind sensor.<ref name="Hyundai Rotem 20170921" /><ref name="sciencetimes-140519" /><ref name="JAKO200734516358474" /> This feature enhances the performance of inexperienced gunners significantly.<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 1"/>

=== Network-centric warfare capabilities and operability ===
==== Tactical information communication ====
[[File:A cold weather combat training of the 11th Division of the ROK Army.webm|thumb|thumbtime=0:55|A cold weather combat training of the tank unit of the [[11th Maneuver Division]] of the [[Republic of Korea Army|ROK Army]]]]

The K2 houses the following features which help to improve situational awareness for the crew:
* [[Command and control#Derivative terms|C4I]] (Command, Control, Communications, Computers, and Intelligence) uplink.<ref name="Hyundai Rotem K2" /><ref name="ADD 1" />
* [[GPS/INS]] (Global Positioning Satellite/Inertial Navigation System) integrated navigation system.<ref name="Hyundai Rotem K2" /><ref name="JAKO200820549300606" /><ref name="Army Technology 20140121">{{cite web|url=https://www.army-technology.com/projects/k2-black-panther-main-battle-tank/|title=K2 Black Panther Main Battle Tank|publisher=Army Technology|date=21 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221206035249/https://www.army-technology.com/projects/k2-black-panther-main-battle-tank/|archive-date=6 December 2022|access-date=6 December 2022|author=}}</ref>
* [[Identification friend or foe|IFF/SIF]] (Identification Friend or Foe/Selective Identification Feature) system compliant with [[Standardization agreement|STANAG 4579]].<ref name="Hyundai Rotem K2" /><ref name="JAKO200820549300606" /><ref name="ADD 1" /> Located on the main gun mantlet, just above the gun, the system fires a 36&nbsp;GHz beam in the direction of the gun for a response from the targeted vehicle. If a proper response signal is shown by the target, the fire control system automatically identifies it as a friendly.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hankyung.com/politics/article/2008081969271|title=3km 밖 전차 적ㆍ아군 구분 꼼짝마! ... 태광이엔시, 초고속식별기개발|publisher=[[Korea Economic Daily]]|date=19 August 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221003175924/https://www.hankyung.com/politics/article/2008081969271|archive-date=3 October 2022|access-date=3 October 2022|author=Lee Gwan-woo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.etnews.com/200808180230|script-title=ko:차기 전차용 피아식별 핵심 모듈 국산화1000억원 수입대체|publisher=Electronic Times Internet|date=19 August 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221003173142/https://www.etnews.com/200808180230|archive-date=3 October 2022|access-date=3 October 2022|author=Ahn Su-min}}</ref> If the target fails to respond to the identification signal, it is then declared as a hostile.
* C4I linked [[Battlefield management system|BMS]] (Battlefield Management System) allows the vehicle to share its data with friendly units, including other [[Armoured fighting vehicle|armored vehicle]]s and [[helicopter]]s.<ref name="Hyundai Rotem K2" /><ref name="JAKO200820549300606" /><ref name="Insopack BMS" /><ref name="ADD 1" />

==== Operability and maintenance ====
The following features are provided for crew operability and system maintenance:
* Network-based tank combat [[training system]] utilizing 3D [[virtual reality]] technology. The embedded training computer designed for the K2 allows [[driving]], gunnery, single tank combat, [[platoon]] level combat and command and platoon leaders combat training, and allows real-time information sharing and training with friendly tanks through a network system.<ref name="Hyundai Rotem K2" /><ref name="Army Technology 20140121" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://koreascience.kr/article/JAKO200826055835387.pdf|title=Development of Network Based Tank Combat Training Model|publisher=[[Agency for Defense Development]]|date=31 December 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230115131558/https://koreascience.kr/article/JAKO200826055835387.pdf|archive-date=15 January 2023|access-date=15 January 2023|author=Roh Keun-lae and Kim Eui-whan}}</ref><ref name="Hyundai Rotem 191023">{{cite web|url=https://blog.hyundai-rotem.co.kr/367|script-title=ko:현대로템의 앞선 방위산업 기술력, ADEX 2019에서 증명하다|publisher=[[Hyundai Rotem]]|date=23 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230311125843/https://blog.hyundai-rotem.co.kr/367|archive-date=11 March 2023|access-date=11 March 2023|author=}}</ref>
* [[Built-in self-test|Built-in test]] (BIT) feature to verify the integrity of the tank system. The BIT system provides the convenience of checking the tank for defects in its main functions without any external [[test equipment]].<ref name="Army Technology 20140121" /><ref name="Hyundai Rotem 191023" />

Work is also under way to integrate the [[XAV|experimental autonomous vehicle]], unmanned wheeled reconnaissance drone into the Black Panther's systems, giving the tank's crew the ability to scout without disclosing its location.

=== Defensive capabilities ===
==== Passive protection systems ====
{{multiple image|perrow = 2|total_width=220|direction=vertical
| image1 = Polish Army K2 turret front Radom-2023.jpg
| image2 = Polish Army K2 right side Radom-2023.jpg
| footer = Reactive armor on the upper and sides
}}

Despite South Korea producing K1 tanks, a dispatched team from the GDLS installed [[Chobham armour|Special Armor Package]] (SAP) to prevent Koreans from physically accessing the Special Armor Package, which was identical to that of the M1 Abrams, in order to protect the United States' intellectual property rights and national security. Armor for main battle tanks was commonly regarded as top secret and its technology was unlikely to be exported. Therefore, developing domestic armor was the only option in order to design a tank.<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 3"/> The ADD and [[Samyang Comtech]] developed [[K1 88-Tank#Protection|Korean Special Armor Package]] (KSAP) for the K1A1 project, and South Korea also keeps most information in military secret level 2.<ref name="Samyang Comtech Accomplishments" /><ref name="KIDET 2020-11">{{cite web|url=http://kidet.or.kr/webzine/2011/09.php|title=K계열 전차 장갑의 성능개량 필요성과 기술추세|publisher=The Korean Institute of Defense Technology|date=November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210419122250/http://kidet.or.kr/webzine/2011/09.php|archive-date=19 April 2021|access-date=19 April 2021|author=Seo Ho-geun}}</ref><ref name="Samyang Comtech">{{cite web|url=http://samyangct.com/eng/lab/?ckattempt=1|title=Special Armor Plate for K1A1 Tank, K2 Tank, Altay Tank|publisher=[[Samyang Comtech]]|access-date=2 September 2022|author=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wqsEJicbwyY|title=방호력의 끝판왕 K2전차 장갑(裝甲) ◀방산톡톡▶ 국방홍보원|publisher=Defense Media Agency|date=12 May 2025|archiveurl=https://preservetube.com/watch?v=wqsEJicbwyY|archivedate=17 August 2026|accessdate=17 August 2026|author1=KFN Defense News}}</ref> In 1996, South Korea received 1,250&nbsp;hp variant Russian domestic specification [[T-80|T-80U]]s along with [[Kontakt-5]] [[Reactive armour#Explosive reactive armour|explosive reactive armor]] (ERA), and studied its composite armor and ERA technology, which contributed to development of domestic armors.<ref name="kookbang 20190524">{{cite web|url=https://kookbang.dema.mil.kr/newsWeb/20190527/1/BBSMSTR_000000010376/view.do|script-title=ko:차관급 다수 편성, 대외 협력시 격 더 올라가|publisher=Korea Defense Daily|date=24 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221211091324/https://kookbang.dema.mil.kr/newsWeb/20190527/1/BBSMSTR_000000010376/view.do|archive-date=11 December 2022|access-date=11 December 2022|author=Kim Min-jeong}}</ref><ref name="kookbang 20210622">{{cite web|url=https://kookbang.dema.mil.kr/newsWeb/20210623/1/BBSMSTR_000000100121/view.do|script-title=ko:두 개의 안테나·4색 위장 무늬... 디테일이 살아있다|publisher=Korea Defense Daily|date=22 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221211091641/https://kookbang.dema.mil.kr/newsWeb/20210623/1/BBSMSTR_000000100121/view.do|archive-date=11 December 2022|access-date=11 December 2022|author=Kang Sin-geum}}</ref>

The K2 uses a [[Modular design|modular]] armor system in order to replace the inner material much quicker when it is damaged or whenever an enhanced version is available.<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Part 1"/><ref name="KIDET 2020-11" /> Its armor was redesigned based on K1A1's KSAP, and is made of [[POSCO]] MIL-12560H armor steel,<ref name="Meta-Defense.fr" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://newsroom.posco.com/kr/%ED%8F%AC%EC%8A%A4%EC%BD%94%EC%97%90%EB%8F%84-bts%EA%B0%80-%EC%9E%88%EB%8B%A4/|script-title=ko:포스코에도 BTS가 있다|publisher=[[POSCO]]|date=23 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220417004833/https://newsroom.posco.com/kr/%ED%8F%AC%EC%8A%A4%EC%BD%94%EC%97%90%EB%8F%84-bts%EA%B0%80-%EC%9E%88%EB%8B%A4/|archive-date=17 April 2022|access-date=17 April 2022|author=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.subcomsolutions.com/assets/pdf/POSCO-Armour-Plates.pdf|title=POSCO Armour Plates|publisher=Subcom Solution|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220417011756/https://www.subcomsolutions.com/assets/pdf/POSCO-Armour-Plates.pdf|archive-date=17 April 2022|access-date=17 April 2022|author=}}</ref> Samyang Comtech [[silicon carbide]] (SiC) [[Ceramic armor|ceramic]] plates, and [[aluminum]] (Al).<ref name="Samyang Comtech" /><ref name="Samyang Comtech 2">{{cite web|url=http://samyangct.com/eng/biz-4/?ckattempt=1|title=Non Oxide Ceramics (SiC)|publisher=[[Samyang Comtech]]|access-date=3 September 2022|author=}}</ref> The frontal armor has been claimed to be effective against the 120&nbsp;mm APFSDS round fired from the [[CN08 120 mm gun|L55]] gun.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://medium.com/war-is-boring/south-koreas-low-rider-tank-is-the-ultimate-mountain-fighting-vehicle-aa78733a512f|title=South Korea’s ‘Low Rider’ Tank Is the Ultimate Mountain Fighting Vehicle|publisher=War Is Boring|date=26 February 2017|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170527025032/https://medium.com/war-is-boring/south-koreas-low-rider-tank-is-the-ultimate-mountain-fighting-vehicle-aa78733a512f|archivedate=27 May 2017|accessdate=27 May 2017|author1=Ed Kim}}</ref> ERA blocks are also present, with the formerly planned addition of ultra-high hardness and high-hardness armor package and [[non-explosive reactive armor]] (NERA) for the K2 Product Improvement Program (PIP) and export variant specification.

According to information provided to the National Defense Committee’s Audit of Government Operations in 2024, the K2's armor is expected to provide protection against the North Korean Bulsae-4 missile (a variant of the [[9K111 Fagot|9M111]]) with an estimated 600 to 800 mm penetration at front, but not at the sides.<ref name="NationalAssemblyHearing2024">{{cite news |author1=한기호 위원 |title=2024년도국감-국방(부록)(2024년10월17일) 1 / 2024 National Assembly Oversight Hearing—Defense (Appendix) (October 17, 2024) 1 |date=17 October 2024 |pages=30-31}}</ref> The more powerful Bulsae-5 missile (a North Korean variant of the [[9M133 Kornet]]) with an estimated 1,000 to 1,200 mm penetration is expected to penetrate even the K2's frontal armor.<ref name="NationalAssemblyHearing2024" /> This matches informations provided by Rep. Han Gi-ho of the [[People Power Party]] in 2021, who claimed that according to internal data of the South Korean military, the frontal armor of the K1 and K2 tanks can be defeated by the Bulsae-5 missile.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Seung-jae |first1=Kim |title=[단독] 北 신형 대전차 미사일 '불새5' 우리軍 전차 다 뚫는다 |url=https://www.chosun.com/politics/2022/09/27/X4VZVTLJH5GB7INDFWKFHUDDN4/ |website=Chosun.com |access-date=16 August 2026 |language=Korean |date=27 September 2022}}</ref>

As per the National Defence Committee, the frontal armor of the K2 provides protection equivalent to 900 mm RHA against shaped charge warheads, whereas the side armor with ERA provides protection equivalent to 330 mm RHA.<ref name="NationalAssemblyHearing2024" /> Subsequently, in 2024 the South Korean Ministry of National Defense requested the budget to incorporate a hard-kill active protection system into the tank.<ref name="NationalAssemblyHearing2024" />

Inside the hull, an [[Overpressure (CBRN protection)|overpressure]] system is installed to protect the tank crew from [[chemical weapon|chemical]] and [[biological agent|biological]] weapons,<ref name="SG Safety 1">{{cite web|url=http://www.sgsafety.net/en/safety/rnd_exports.html|title=Major Development Performance|publisher=SG Safety [[automatic fire suppression]] system is programmed to detect and put out any internal fires that may occur, and atmospheric sensors alert the crew if the tank enters a hazardous environment.<ref ==== Active protection systems ====
[[File:K2 Black Panther tank firing while maneuvering.webm|thumb|left|thumbtime=0:03|K2 tanks deploy K415 smoke grenades and fire during maneuver drills.]]

The tank is equipped with [[Radar warning receiver|Radar Warning Receiver]] (RWR) and [[Laser warning receiver|Laser Warning Receiver]] (LWR), which detect [[Active radar homing|homing radar]] or [[Laser guidance#Military use|homing laser]] aimed at the tank and instantaneously turn the turret in the direction of threats<ref name="dema">{{cite web|url=http://www.mnd.go.kr/user/boardList.action?command=view&page=1&boardId=O_47261&boardSeq=O_104438&titleId=null&id=mnd_eng_030100000000|title=True worth of masterwork, "great power" during performance demonstration|publisher=[[Ministry of National Defense (South Korea)|Ministry of National Defense]]|date=8 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141016214630/http://www.mnd.go.kr/user/boardList.action?command=view&page=1&boardId=O_47261&boardSeq=O_104438&titleId=null&id=mnd_eng_030100000000|archive-date=16 October 2014|access-date=16 October 2014|author=Kim Chul-Hwan}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://armynuri.tistory.com/1033|script-title=ko:실전 배치된 K-2전차의 위용|publisher=Armynuri|date=19 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220930210953/https://armynuri.tistory.com/1033|archive-date=30 September 2022|access-date=30 September 2022|author=Jeong Seung-ik}}</ref> as well as notifying friendly units via network system.<ref name="KR101662443B1">{{cite web|url=https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/60/c6/ab/e1d31f9084fc10/KR101662443B1.pdf|title=레이저 수신방향 측정 공유 장치|publisher=[[Korean Intellectual Property Office]]|date=27 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250712004933/https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/60/c6/ab/e1d31f9084fc10/KR101662443B1.pdf|archive-date=12 July 2025|access-date=12 July 2025|author1=[[Hyundai Rotem]]}}</ref> The tank also has a total of 12 (6 on each side of the turret) [[Samyang Chemical]] K415 Visible/IR Screening Smoke Grenade. The K415 blocks visible and infrared view of the K2 from the enemy.<ref name="Samyang Chemical Ammunition">{{cite web|url=https://samyangchem.com/en/product_03-en/?ckattempt=3|title=Ammunition|publisher=Samyang Chemical|date=2026|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/8IEHy|archivedate=16 August 2026|accessdate=16 August 2026|author1=}}</ref>

The K2 has a [[Multispectral]] Screening Smoke Grenade (MSSG) soft-kill [[active protection system]].{{notetag|In Korea, this soft-kill active protection system is commonly called multi-region screening smoke grenade ({{Korean|hangul=다영역차장 연막유탄|labels=no}}).}} If an [[anti-tank guided missile]] (ATGM) is fired at the K2, the tank immediately warns crews and triangulate the projectile for activating [[SNT Dynamics]] SLS (Soft-kill Launcher System)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hisntd.com/eng/business/data/Protecion_Weapons.pdf|title=Protection Weapons|publisher=[[SNT p. 12</ref> that releases K419 multispectral screening smoke grenade,<ref name="Samyang Chemical Ammunition" /> manufactured by Samyang Chemical, in the direction of the incoming missile at the most effective time.<ref name="XT2-2010-1417">{{cite from [[Visible spectrum|visible]], [[forward-looking infrared]], and [[Extremely high frequency|millimeter wave]] optics and radar thus disrupt accuracy of missile.<ref name="K2 Developers Interview Development]]}}</ref>

The SLS is located at the rear center of the turret top, and is assisted by two [[Missile approach warning system#Pulse-Doppler–based MAW|Missile Warning Receiver]] (MWR) on the frontal turret using L-band pulsed doppler radar. Each system covers 90 degrees (total 180 degrees) and 60 degrees at a high angle, and is capable of detecting [[wire-guided missile]]s, which does not emit its own radar.<ref name="JAKO200925265919312" /> The MWR will also be responsible for tracking and targeting incoming missiles for the hard-kill active protection system in future upgrades.

=== Mobility and maneuverability ===
The K2 can travel at speeds of up to {{convert|70|km/h|abbr=on}} on road surfaces, accelerate from {{convert|0|to|32|km/h|abbr=on}} within 7.47 seconds (MT883 Ka-501 engine) or 8.77 seconds (DV27K engine),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hankyung.com/politics/article/2014111159461|script-title=ko:"흑표전차 국산 파워팩, 독일제와 성능 대등"|publisher=[[Korea Economic Daily]]|date=11 November 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221001093321/https://www.hankyung.com/politics/article/2014111159461|archive-date=1 October 2022|access-date=1 October 2022|author=Choi Seung-uk}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hankookilbo.com/News/Read/201409260452636553|script-title=ko:"탱크 가속성능 기준 완화" 軍, K2 국산화 완료 가닥|publisher=[[Hankook Ilbo]]|date=26 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221001184330/https://www.hankookilbo.com/News/Read/201409260452636553|archive-date=1 October 2022|access-date=1 October 2022|author=Kim Gwang-su}}</ref> and maintain speeds of up to {{convert|50|km/h|abbr=on}} in off-road conditions. It can also climb 60% slopes (31 degrees) and vertical obstacles 1.3 meters in height.<ref name="Bemil 20211015" /> Due to the relatively compact design of the engine, the designers were able to fit an additional compact [[auxiliary power unit|Auxiliary Power Unit]] (APU)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tzen.co.kr/english/product/product3.html|title=Auxiliary Power Units(APU)|publisher=Farymann & TZEN|date=2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220307115325/http://www.tzen.co.kr/english/product/product3.html|archive-date=7 March 2022|access-date=7 March 2022|author=Farymann & TZEN}}</ref> into the remaining compartment space. This is capable of producing 8~10&nbsp;kW, and intended to act as an auxiliary power unit with which the tank may power its on-board systems when its main engine is turned off. It will also allow the tank to conserve fuel when idling and minimize the vehicle's thermal and acoustic signatures.

==== In-arm Suspension Unit (ISU) ====
[[File:K2 Black Panther tank demonstrating the posture control function of the in-arm suspension unit at the Gyeryong Ground Forces Cultural Festival 2016.webm|thumbtime=0:09|thumb|K2 demonstrating posture control function]]

The Black Panther fields an advanced semi-active suspension system, called the ''in-arm suspension unit'' (ISU),<ref name="Hyundai Rotem K2" /> which allows for individual control of every bogie on the tracks. This posture control function can tilt the [[chassis]] or lower the overall height by {{convert|40|cm|in|sp=us}}.<ref name="dema" /> This allows the K2 to "sit", "stand" and "kneel", as well as "lean" towards one side or a corner. "Sitting" gives the tank a lower profile and offers superior handling over roads. "Standing" gives the vehicle higher ground clearance for maneuverability over rough terrain.<ref name="Hyundai Rotem 20170921" /> "Kneeling" augments the angular range in which the tank's gun barrel can elevate and depress, allowing the vehicle to fire its main gun downhill as well as engage low-flying aircraft more effectively. The [[height adjustable suspension]] system detects rough road surface conditions in real time through the movement of the first road wheel in front and collects data, and the five road wheels in the rear automatically control the hydraulic pressure of the in-arm suspension unit and [[Magnetorheological damper|variable damper]] based on this terrain data to maintain optimal driving performance.<ref name="KRIS 2019-10-11" />

The unique suspension system of the Black Panther expands the gun's elevation angles, allowing it to target from a high hill or a low valley. This makes it particularly effective in mountainous areas with steep hills or even in urban cities with tall buildings. K2 can elevate its main gun up to 24 degrees, which allows a curved trajectory attack at a hovering helicopter target {{convert|5|km|mi|sp=us}} away.<ref name="Seoul Shinmun 20141003" /> The suspension system also cushions the chassis from vibrations when traveling over uneven terrain, as the bogies can be individually adjusted on the fly. This contributes to the comfort and overall condition of the operators engaged in fierce battles. The compact in-arm suspension unit with the integration of [[gas spring]]s and dampers is mounted independently on the side of the chassis to provide additional interior space.<ref name="Hyundai Rotem 2020-05-22">{{cite web|url=https://hyundai-rotem.tistory.com/444|title=K1A2·K1E1, 성능개량으로 강해지는 전차!|publisher=[[Hyundai Rotem]]|date=22 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240601005717/https://hyundai-rotem.tistory.com/444|archive-date=1 June 2024|access-date=1 June 2024|author1=}}</ref>

The K2 also has advanced track system called Dynamic Track Tension System (DTTS). Maintaining optimum tension through all maneuvers, it dramatically reduces the chance of throwing a track even in the most extreme situations. The DTTS is also designed to maintain optimal track tension while K2 is maneuvering to minimize the excessive load on the track and prevent the track from peeling off the road wheels.<ref name="Mottrol" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://koreascience.kr/article/JAKO200111920908908.pdf|title=Development of a Dynamic Track Tensioning System in Tracked Vehicles|publisher=The Korean Society of Mechanical Engineers|date=1 October 2001|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221230073738/https://koreascience.kr/article/JAKO200111920908908.pdf|archive-date=30 December 2022|access-date=30 December 2022|author1=Mun-suk Suh|author2=Kunsoo Huh|author3=Daegun Hong|author4=Choonho Lee|author5=Philwhan Choi}}</ref>

==== Snorkel System ====
[[File:20사단 남한강 혹한기 훈련- (2) (24146074099).jpg|thumb|K2 tank fording a shallow river]]
[[File:2014_%EB%8C%80%ED%95%9C%EB%AF%BC%EA%B5%AD_%EB%B0%A9%EC%9C%84%EC%82%B0%EC%97%85%EC%A0%84%28DX_Korea%29_%EC%9C%A1%EA%B5%B0%EC%9D%98_%EB%AA%85%ED%92%88_%EB%AC%B4%EA%B8%B0%EC%99%80_%EC%9E%A5%EB%B9%84_%EC%86%8C%EA%B0%9C_%2815556786856%29.jpg|thumb|K2 tank with snorkel]]

The K2 Black Panther is a unique tank equipped with advanced snorkel capabilities, enabling it to navigate challenging battlefields with numerous rivers. It is fully protected from biochemical attacks by a sealed and air circulation system. This allows the tank to independently cross rivers and reach the battlefield faster than others that require engineers to build bridges or boats for river crossings. The vehicle can cross rivers as deep as 4.1 meters using a [[Vehicle snorkel|snorkel system]],<ref name="Hyundai Rotem K2" /> which also serves as a [[conning tower]] for the tank commander. The system takes approximately 20–30 minutes to prepare.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blog.hyundai-rotem.co.kr/432|script-title=ko:전투차량인가 잠수함인가? 물속도 누비는 전투차량 총정리|publisher=[[Hyundai Rotem]]|date=13 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221001004505/https://blog.hyundai-rotem.co.kr/432|archive-date=1 October 2022|access-date=1 October 2022|author=}}</ref><ref name="Seoul Shinmun 20141003">{{cite web|url=https://www.seoul.co.kr/news/newsView.php?id=20141003500213|script-title=ko:[신인균의 밀리터리 르포] K-2흑표전차와 기동군단|publisher=[[Seoul Shinmun]]|date=3 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221001190451/https://www.seoul.co.kr/news/newsView.php?id=20141003500213|archive-date=1 October 2022|access-date=1 October 2022|author=Shin In-gyun}}</ref> The turret becomes watertight while fording, but the chassis can take in {{convert|500|USgal|L|order=flip|sp=us}} of water to prevent excessive buoyancy from air inside the vehicle and keep the tracks planted firmly on the ground. Furthermore, the tank can enter combat-ready status as soon as it resurfaces. It is said that K2's predecessor, K1, can cross a river of 2 meter depth after 2 hours of preparation, which also requires assistance from military engineers. However, a K2 tank does not require outside assistance for river crossing.<ref name="Seoul Shinmun 20141003" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://m.khan.co.kr/politics/politics-general/article/201604191026001|script-title=ko:육군 K-2 흑표전차, 남한강서 잠수도하 훈련|publisher=[[Kyunghyang Shinmun]]|date=19 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221001193239/https://m.khan.co.kr/politics/politics-general/article/201604191026001|archive-date=1 October 2022|access-date=1 October 2022|author=Park Seong-jin}}</ref> This type of self water-crossing ability is beneficial from a tactical perspective, as it allows for more attacking routes.

==== Engines and powertrains ====
In March 2011, South Korean [[Defense Acquisition Program Administration]] (DAPA) announced that mass production of the K2, which the Army was expecting to deploy in 2012, would not happen due to problems concerning its engine and transmission.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/news/nation/2011/03/116_83997.html|title=Made-in-Korea arms struggle with defects|publisher=[[The Korea Times]]|date=28 March 2011|author=Lee Tae-hoon|access-date=29 March 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121002074000/http://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/news/nation/2011/03/116_83997.html|archive-date=2 October 2012|url-status=live}}</ref> In the evaluation test conducted in March 2012, it was reported that the domestic powerpack did not meet the required operational capability (ROC) proposed by the [[Ministry of National Defense (South Korea)|Ministry of National Defense]] in three categories: cooling fan speed control, maximum power at low temperature, and acceleration performance.<ref name="Chosun20120329">{{cite web|url=https://www.chosun.com/site/data/html_dir/2012/03/30/2012033000173.html|script-title=ko:[단독] 1200억 투자한 K-2 전차 파워팩 국산화, 결국 실패|publisher=[[The Chosun Ilbo]]|date=29 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220928030929/https://www.chosun.com/site/data/html_dir/2012/03/30/2012033000173.html|archive-date=28 September 2022|access-date=28 September 2022|author=Jeon Hyeon-seok}}</ref>

In April 2012, DAPA announced that due to ongoing issues with the reliability and durability of the domestically produced powerpack, the first 100 production K2s would use German-made [[EuroPowerPack|Euro Powerpack]] and that service entry would be delayed until March 2014.<ref name="koreatimes20120402">{{cite web|url=https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/news/nation/2012/04/116_108229.html|title=Korea to buy German engines for K2 tanks|publisher=[[The Korea Times]]|date=2 April 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220928042845/http://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/news/nation/2012/04/116_108229.html|archive-date=28 September 2022|access-date=28 September 2022|url-status=live|author=Lee Tae-hoon}}</ref> The first 15 K2 Black Panther tanks were put into service in June 2014. Faulty domestic engines and transmissions previously halted production, but the lowering of required acceleration performance allowed it to enter service.{{citation needed|date=November 2025}} Until domestic [[Doosan|Doosan Infracore]] (now HD Hyundai Infracore) 1,500&nbsp;hp engines were produced, the first mass production was employed with a German-made MTU powerpack, which was able to produce 100 vehicles by 2015.<ref name="Hyundai 20201222" />

Hyundai Rotem signed a contract from the second batch of 106 K2 tanks in December 2014, but the vehicles continued to have powerpack issues due to the domestic [[SNT Dynamics]] transmission failing durability tests. After SNT Dynamics complained about the domestic powerpack test standards, the 107th Defense Acquisition Program Promotion Committee held on November 29, 2017, gave it an opportunity to retest the durability of the transmission, but SNT Dynamics refused to retest the durability of the transmission.<ref name="nascomm 2017">{{cite web|url=https://defense.na.go.kr:444/flexer/upload/nascomm/_attach/file/2018/07/xlvfmkHRXFNMFyaUBdRi.hwp.files/Sections1.html|script-title=ko:2017년도 국정감사결과 시정 및 처리 요구사항에 대한 처리결과보고서|publisher=National Defense Committee|date=April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220927135130/https://defense.na.go.kr:444/flexer/upload/nascomm/_attach/file/2018/07/xlvfmkHRXFNMFyaUBdRi.hwp.files/Sections1.html|archive-date=27 September 2022|access-date=27 September 2022|author=}} p. 147–148</ref> In February 2018, DAPA announced the second batch would have a "hybrid" powerpack consisting of the locally developed engine with the German [[Renk|RENK]] transmission system, allowing them to start entering service in 2019. An additional contract for the production of a third batch of about 110 K2s is to follow within the next several years.<ref name="defensenews20180214">{{cite web|url=https://www.defensenews.com/global/asia-pacific/2018/02/14/south-koreas-k2-tank-to-run-on-german-transmission/|title=South Korea's K2 tank to run on German transmission|publisher=Defense News|date=14 February 2018|access-date=19 March 2018|author=Jeff Jeong}}</ref>

On 25 November 2020, the 131st Defense Acquisition Program Promotion Committee decided to produce tanks in a powerpack that combines domestic engines and German transmissions in the third batch because SNT Dynamics refused to retest the durability of the domestic transmission.<ref name="asiae20201126">{{cite web|url=https://www.asiae.co.kr/article/2020112609112398255|title=K-2전차, 국산 변속기 결국 포기|publisher=Asia Economy|date=26 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220927161223/https://www.asiae.co.kr/article/2020112609112398255|archive-date=27 September 2022|access-date=27 September 2022|author=Yang Nak-gyu}}</ref>

On 6 December 2021, a senior SNT Dynamics official said it solved a technical problem with the transmission defect, and only the Ministry of National Defense's durability test remains in the first half of next year, and the fourth production of the K2 tank will include domestic transmission.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20211206000824|script-title=ko:[단독] SNT중공업, K2 전차 "변속기 문제 해결, 4차 물량에 들어갈 것"|publisher=[[The Korea Herald]]|date=6 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220315164433/http://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20211206000824|archive-date=15 March 2022|access-date=15 March 2022|author=Kim Byung-wook}}</ref>

== K2 product improvement program (K2 PIP) ==

The K2 PIP is an improved version of the initial production model of the K2. Improvements will include:
* Upgraded modular [[vehicle armour|armor package]] made of ultra-high hardness and high-hardness armor steel combining [[nanotechnology]], developed for the K2 export variant.<ref name="Samyang Comtech Accomplishments" /><ref name="Samyang Comtech History" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.add.re.kr/board/view?pageNum=1&rowCnt=10&linkId=5252&menuId=MENU02226&schType=0&boardStyle=&categoryId=&continent=&country=&schText=|script-title=ko:고경도 및 초고경도 철강 장갑판재 기술 개발로 방탄성능 개선에 기여|publisher=[[Agency for Defense Development]]|date=8 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220524161223/https://www.add.re.kr/board/view?pageNum=1&rowCnt=10&linkId=5252&menuId=MENU02226&schType=0&boardStyle=&categoryId=&continent=&country=&schText=|archive-date=24 May 2022|access-date=24 May 2022|author=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dapa.go.kr/common/nttFileDownload.do?fileKey=b997cfd178b97c5e665f686d12a5f24d|script-title=ko:국방과학연구소, 고경도 및 초고경도 철강 장갑 판재 기술 개발로 방탄성능 개선에 기여|publisher=[[Defense Acquisition Program Administration]]|date=8 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220503065502/https://www.dapa.go.kr/common/nttFileDownload.do?fileKey=b997cfd178b97c5e665f686d12a5f24d|archive-date=3 May 2022|access-date=3 May 2022|author=}}</ref>
* Upgrading the semi-active in-arm suspension unit to an active in-arm suspension unit.
* Integration of a high-resolution terrain-scanning system to the vehicle's suspension system. This is purported to allow the vehicle to "plan ahead" by scanning nearby terrain up to 50 meters away in all directions and calculate the optimal position of the bogies in order to improve vehicle handling over uneven terrain.
* Integration of a hard-kill [[active protection system]].
* Addition of [[non-explosive reactive armor]].
* Potentially replacing the 120&nbsp;mm / L55 gun with an [[Electrothermal-chemical technology|electrothermal-chemical gun]], which will significantly increase the vehicle's firepower and potential payload.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://koreascience.or.kr/article/JAKO201231434112066.pdf|title=150 kJ Compact Capacitive Pulsed Power System for an Electrothermal Chemical Gun|publisher=[[Agency for Defense Development]]|date=1 November 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220412010349/http://koreascience.or.kr/article/JAKO201231434112066.pdf|archive-date=12 April 2022|access-date=12 April 2022|author=Byungha Lee}}</ref> Later, the plan was scrapped because ADD succeeded in developing a new desensitized propellant for 120&nbsp;mm munition.

=== Korean Active Protection System (KAPS) ===
The [[KAPS (countermeasure)|Korean Active Protection System]] (KAPS) is an indigenously developed hard-kill active protection system designed to protect the K2 from anti-tank threats. It uses a three-dimensional detection and tracking radar and a thermal imager to detect incoming threats.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://koreascience.or.kr/article/JAKO201124359116046.pdf|title=Method of MBT Movement Modeling for Performance Analysis of SRMD System|publisher=Journal of the Korea Institute of Military Science and Technology|date=5 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209091649/https://koreascience.or.kr/article/JAKO201124359116046.pdf|archive-date=9 February 2022|access-date=9 February 2022|author=[[Agency for Defense Development]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|url=https://koreascience.kr/article/JAKO201424750260755.pdf|title=Methodology of System Alignment using Angular Error Compensation Among Multi-Axes|journal=Journal of the Korea Institute of Military Science and Technology|date=5 June 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220807010214/https://koreascience.kr/article/JAKO201424750260755.pdf|issn=1598-9127|volume=17|number=3|pages=342–349|archive-date=7 August 2022|access-date=7 August 2022|author=[[Agency for Defense Development]]|doi=10.9766/KIMST.2014.17.3.342 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.koreascience.or.kr/article/JAKO201424750260757.pdf|title=Performance Analysis of Missile/Rocket Defense System for RPG-7 Defense of Main Battle Tank|journal=Journal of the Korea Institute of Military Science and Technology|date=5 June 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209080953/https://www.koreascience.or.kr/article/JAKO201424750260757.pdf|issn=1598-9127|volume=17|number=3|pages=350–357|archive-date=9 February 2022|access-date=9 February 2022|author=Agency for Defense Development|doi=10.9766/KIMST.2014.17.3.350 }}</ref> Warheads can be detected out to 150 meters from the tank, and a defensive rocket is fired to destroy them at 10–15 meters away.<ref name="yna">{{cite web|url=https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20120228120100043|title=軍, 대전차미사일 자동추적ㆍ파괴체계 개발|date=28 February 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209095035/https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20120228120100043|archive-date=9 February 2022|access-date=9 February 2022|author=Kim Ho-jun|work=[[Yonhap News Agency]] }}</ref><ref name="ktv">{{cite web|url=https://www.ktv.go.kr/content/view?content_id=417610|script-title=ko:대전차 미사일 방어용 '능동파괴체계' 개발|publisher=KTV|date=28 February 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209035747/https://www.ktv.go.kr/content/view?content_id=417610|archive-date=9 February 2022|access-date=9 February 2022|author=Kang Pil-seong}}</ref>

The system can neutralize [[rocket-propelled grenade]]s and anti-tank guided missiles. It may be installed on other platforms in the future like warships, helicopters, and buildings. Unit price per system is [[South Korean won|₩]]670 million ($600,000).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.defensenews.com/article/20120228/DEFREG02/302280010/S-Korea-Develops-Active-Protection-System-Armor|title=S. Korea Develops Active Protection System for Armor|publisher=Defense News|date=28 February 2012|access-date=13 February 2014|author=Jung Sung-ki}}</ref> Implementation of the KAPS was cancelled in 2014 due to budgetary issues along with the price of a K2 being at 8 billion won, with addition of the KAPS it would increase procurement costs by 1 billion won per unit.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hankookilbo.com/News/Read/201409290432359155|script-title=ko:[단독] K2전차, 핵심 방어장비 장착 안 했다|publisher=[[Hankook Ilbo]]|date=29 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220317044002/https://www.hankookilbo.com/News/Read/201409290432359155|archive-date=17 March 2022|access-date=17 March 2022|author=Kim Gwang-su}}</ref>
