== Exports ==
=== Turkey ===
{{See also|Altay (tank)}}
[[File:Altay Tank.jpg|thumb|right|Altay T1]]

In June 2007, South Korea and Turkey negotiated an arms deal worth ₩500 billion (approximately $540 million), which included South Korea's support in the development of Turkey's Altay main battle tank and the export of 40 (+15) [[KAI KT-1 Woongbi|KT-1]] trainer aircraft to Turkey.<ref name="Chosun Ilbo 070622">{{cite web|url=http://english.chosun.com/w21data/html/news/200706/200706220024.html |title=Korea in Huge Arms Export Deal to Turkey |publisher=[[The Chosun Ilbo]] |access-date=2009-08-09 |date=2007-06-22 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090621213807/http://english.chosun.com/w21data/html/news/200706/200706220024.html |archive-date=June 21, 2009 }}</ref>

On July 29, 2008, Hyundai Rotem and Turkey's [[Otokar]] signed a contract to provide design assistance and technology transfer for the Altay tank project. This collaboration included critical design elements, systems integration, and manufacturing expertise from South Korea, specifically tailored to develop Turkey's domestic manufacturing capabilities.<ref name="Export1">{{cite web|url=https://www.hyundai-rotem.co.kr/PRCenter/News_View.asp?type=%EC%96%B8%EB%A1%A0%EB%B3%B4%EB%8F%84&idx=1415&ref=|script-title=ko:터키 전차개발 기술협력 계약 체결|publisher=[[Hyundai Rotem]]|date=31 July 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211010183718/https://www.hyundai-rotem.co.kr/PRCenter/News_View.asp?type=%EC%96%B8%EB%A1%A0%EB%B3%B4%EB%8F%84&idx=1415&ref=|archive-date=10 October 2021|access-date=10 October 2021|author=[[Hyundai Rotem]]}}</ref>

South Korean contributions to the Altay's development included the transfer of manufacturing technologies for critical components. Hyundai Rotem played a pivotal role in the system design and integration process, while Hyundai WIA provided the 120&nbsp;mm 55-caliber smoothbore gun technology. Samyang Comtech shared expertise in advanced armor materials, and Poongsan Corporation supported the development of ballistic protection systems. These efforts laid the foundation for Turkey's indigenous capabilities in producing the Altay.<ref name="Export2">{{cite web|url=https://www.hani.co.kr/arti/politics/defense/301490.html|script-title=ko:터키에 한국형 전차 '흑표' 기술 수출|publisher=[[The Hankyoreh]]|date=30 July 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727052911/https://www.hani.co.kr/arti/politics/defense/301490.html|archive-date=27 July 2021|access-date=27 July 2021|author=Son Won-je}}</ref>

The cooperation extended beyond technical support, encompassing assistance in establishing production lines for key subsystems. Hyundai Rotem guided Otokar in tank systems development, while MKEK ([[Mechanical and Chemical Industry Corporation]]) received tank gun production technologies. [[Roketsan]] was supported in the design and manufacturing of advanced armor packages. These collaborative efforts were instrumental in the development of prototypes PV1 and PV2, finalized in 2015, and the Altay project's official completion in 2016.<ref name="Defense Export">{{cite web|url=https://www.add.re.kr/board?menuId=MENU02982&siteId=null|title=Major Export Cases|publisher=[[Agency for Defense Development]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220530033958/https://www.add.re.kr/board?menuId=MENU02982&siteId=null|archive-date=30 May 2022|access-date=30 May 2022|author=}}</ref><ref name="Global Security Altay">{{cite web|url=https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/world/europe/altay.htm|title=Altay National Main Battle Tank of Turkey|publisher=[[GlobalSecurity.org]]|date=2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205130505/https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/world/europe/altay.htm|archive-date=5 February 2022|access-date=5 February 2022|author=}}</ref>

On 10 March 2021, [[BMC Otomotiv|BMC]], the main contractor responsible for the production of Altay tanks, decided to import engines and transmissions from South Korea to address production delays.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.news1.kr/articles/?4235459|script-title=ko:터키 차세대 전차 '알타이'에 '국산파워팩' 수출|publisher=News1 Korea|date=10 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210316123242/https://www.news1.kr/articles/?4235459|archive-date=16 March 2021|access-date=16 March 2021|author=Kim Min-seok}}</ref> Seven months later, on 22 October 2021, South Korea's DAPA approved the export of Hyundai Doosan Infracore (now HD Hyundai Infracore) DV27K engines and SNT Dynamics EST15K transmissions to Turkey.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20211022165300108|script-title=ko:터키 전차에 국산 파워팩 탑재...터키 외무 "수출 승인받아"|publisher=[[Yonhap News Agency]]|date=22 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211025101338/https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20211022165300108|archive-date=25 October 2021|access-date=25 October 2021|author=Kim Seung-uk}}</ref> In August 2022, durability testing of the powerpack, combining the DV27K engine and EST15K transmission from South Korea, was successfully completed. Following this success, the first batch of Altay tanks will be produced using this Korean powerpack, which includes engines from HD Hyundai Infracore and transmissions by SNT Dynamics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.defenceturk.net/altay-tanki-2025de-milli-guc-grubuna-sahip-olacak|title=ALTAY tankı 2025'de milli güç grubuna sahip olacak|publisher=defenceturk|date=11 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220901195406/https://www.defenceturk.net/altay-tanki-2025de-milli-guc-grubuna-sahip-olacak|archive-date=1 September 2022|access-date=1 September 2022|author=Yusuf Emir Işık}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-29 |title=Korean Power Pack for the K2 Tank |url=https://defence24.com/industry/korean-power-pack-for-the-k2-tank |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=Default |language=pl}}</ref>

=== Poland ===
[[File:K2 Tank Joins the Fight with eFP Battle Group Poland - 2.jpg|thumb|right|A Polish K2GF tank, 2023]]
In January 2020, [[Poland]] announced negotiations with Hyundai Rotem for license production of the K2 Black Panther for the [[Polish Army]].<ref name="auto">{{cite web|url=https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/nation/2021/08/205_282115.html|title=Hyundai Rotem favored to land $9 bil. tank deal with Poland|publisher=[[The Korea Times]]|date=17 January 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220609065452/https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/nation/2021/08/205_282115.html|archive-date=9 June 2022|access-date=9 June 2022|author=Kim Hyun-bin}}</ref>

On 13 June 2022, the [[Ministry of National Defence (Poland)|Polish Ministry of Defence]] announced that it had signed a [[memorandum of understanding]] (MoU) to purchase at least 180 K2 tanks for the Polish military. The 180 tanks will be produced by Hyundai Rotem in South Korea starting in 2022 and then supplied to the [[Polish Army]].<ref name=tweet>{{cite tweet |user=mblaszczak |number=1536323043957653504 |title=Wojsko musi być wyposażone w nowoczesny sprzęt |author=Minister Obrony Narodowej |date=13 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220807035020/https://twitter.com/mblaszczak/status/1536323043957653504? |archive-date=7 August 2022 |access-date=7 August 2022}}</ref><ref name=wnp>{{cite web|url=https://www.wnp.pl/przemysl-obronny/polska-kupi-w-korei-mysliwce-fa-50-i-czolgi-k2%2C604965.html|title=Polska kupi w Korei myśliwce FA-50 i czołgi K2|publisher=PRZEMYSŁ OBRONNY|date=22 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220807040035/https://www.wnp.pl/przemysl-obronny/polska-kupi-w-korei-mysliwce-fa-50-i-czolgi-k2,604965.html|archive-date=7 August 2022|access-date=7 August 2022|author=PAP}}</ref>

On 27 July 2022, the [[Polish Armaments Group]] (PGZ) and Hyundai Rotem signed a [[framework agreement]] to supply 180 K2s and 820 K2PLs. The contract includes rapid arms supply and extensive technology transfer from South Korea. 180 K2s will be produced in South Korea and delivered to [[Poland]] starting in 2022 and 820 K2PLs will be produced in Poland under license starting in 2026.<ref name="Dziennik Zbrojny" /><ref name="Polish Ministry of Defence" /><ref name="PGZ" /><ref name="Defence24" />

On 26 August 2022, the first [[executive agreement]] worth $3.37 billion was signed to procure 180 K2s in [[Morąg]], northern Poland. The contract includes training programs, logistics packages, explosive reactive armor packages, 50,000 120&nbsp;mm, 4.3 million [[7.62×51mm NATO|7.62&nbsp;mm]] and [[.50 BMG|12.7&nbsp;mm]] machine gun [[ammunition]] for the K2.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sTbw8J6B7R4|script-title=ko:[단독] 국산 기관총탄 430만 발, 우크라 옆 폴란드 간다 / SBS 8뉴스|publisher=[[Seoul Broadcasting System|SBS]] News|date=19 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230429135811/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sTbw8J6B7R4|archive-date=29 April 2023|access-date=19 April 2023|author=Kim Tae-hoon}}</ref> Soldiers of the [[16th Mechanised Division (Poland)|16th Mechanised Division]] of the Polish Army were sent to South Korea in October 2022 to participate in the training program. The 180 K2 tanks, which will be delivered from 2022 to 2025, will be sequentially deployed to the 20th Mechanised Brigade, 15th Mechanised Brigade and 9th Armoured Cavalry Brigade, which are brigade-class units belonging to the 16th Mechanised Division.<ref name="TVP Info 20221015" /><ref name="Defence24 20220826">{{cite web|url=https://defence24.pl/przemysl/czolgi-haubice-i-amunicja-za-miliardy-juz-w-tym-roku-umowy-wykonawcze-z-korea-podpisane|title=Czołgi, haubice i amunicja za miliardy już w tym roku. Umowy wykonawcze z Koreą podpisane|publisher=Defence24|date=26 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220826165218/https://defence24.pl/przemysl/czolgi-haubice-i-amunicja-za-miliardy-juz-w-tym-roku-umowy-wykonawcze-z-korea-podpisane|archive-date=26 August 2022|access-date=26 August 2022|author=JAKUB PALOWSKI}}</ref><ref name="YTN 20220827">{{cite web|url=https://www.ytn.co.kr/_ln/0101_202208270319376864|script-title=ko:폴란드와 K2 전차·K9 자주포 7조6천억 규모 계약 체결|publisher=[[YTN]]|date=27 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220826232858/https://www.ytn.co.kr/_ln/0101_202208270319376864|archive-date=26 August 2022|access-date=26 August 2022|author=Shin Jun-myeong}}</ref>

On 7 September 2022, PGZ and Hyundai Rotem signed a [[Partnership#Partnership agreements|partnership agreement]] to develop and produce tanks, armored vehicles and ground unmanned systems. The contract includes joint cooperation in building manufacturing facilities in Poland for the production and maintenance of 1000 K2s and the production of K3 next-generation main battle tanks. In addition, the facility to be built in [[Poland]] will be used as a hub in [[Europe]] for the sale and maintenance of Hyundai Rotem's tanks and armored vehicles.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://grupapgz.pl/pgz-i-hyundai-rotem-podpisuja-memorandum-o-partnerstwie/|title=PGZ i Hyundai Rotem podpisały memorandum o partnerstwie|publisher=[[Polish Armaments Group|PGZ]]|date=7 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220909225830/https://grupapgz.pl/pgz-i-hyundai-rotem-podpisuja-memorandum-o-partnerstwie/|archive-date=9 September 2022|access-date=9 September 2022|author=}}</ref>
[[File:Polish Army K2 at Radom-2023.jpg|thumb|right|K2 at Radom, Poland (2023)]]

On 5 December 2022, the first 10 K2s arrived  in Poland, just "six months" following the signing of the agreement.<ref name="Defence24 20221205" /><ref name="Dziennik Zbrojny 20221206" /> They were delivered to the 20th Mechanised Brigade of the 16th Mechanised Division on 9 December 2022.<ref name="Wojsko Polskie 20221209" /><ref name="zbiam 20221209" />

On 31 March 2023, the [[Polish Ministry of Defense]] signed a [[foundational agreement]] with Hyundai Rotem for a [[consortium]] to produce K2PL in [[Poznań]]. The agreement included a supply of K2PL, which was redesigned to meet the Polish military's requirements, and a support vehicle based on the K2PL's platform.<ref name="Defence24 2023-04-03">{{cite web|url=https://defence24.com/industry/polish-korean-consortium-created-k2-tanks-to-be-manufactured-in-poznan|title=Polish-Korean Consortium Created. K2 Tanks to be Manufactured in Poznan|publisher=Defence24|date=3 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230422132040/https://defence24.com/industry/polish-korean-consortium-created-k2-tanks-to-be-manufactured-in-poznan|archive-date=22 April 2023|access-date=23 April 2023|author=Damian Ratka}}</ref>

Following the [[Russian invasion of Ukraine]], the K2 Black Panther became a central component of Poland's military modernisation programme through a series of large-scale defence agreements with [[South Korea]].<ref>{{cite news |date=12 May 2026 |title=Poland second biggest arms importer in Europe |url=https://tvpworld.com/91992072/poland-second-biggest-arms-importer-in-europe |work=TVP World}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=9 March 2026 |title=Global arms flows jump nearly 10 per cent as European demand soars |url=https://www.sipri.org/media/press-release/2026/global-arms-flows-jump-nearly-10-cent-european-demand-soars |website=SIPRI}}</ref> Largely supported by the EU, Poland ordered hundreds of K2 tanks as part of efforts to rapidly expand and modernise the [[Polish Armed Forces]] and reinforce NATO's eastern flank.<ref>{{cite news |date=8 March 2026 |title=Europe now world's biggest arms importer, think tank says |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/europe-now-worlds-biggest-arms-importer-think-tank-says-2026-03-08/ |work=Reuters}}</ref>

The Polish contracts contributed to the growing international profile of South Korea's defence industry, with [[SIPRI]] identifying the country as an increasingly significant global arms exporter during the 2021–2026 period.

=== Failed bids ===
==== Norway ====
The [[Norwegian Army]] considered the K2 (assigned as the K2NO) in a 2020 bid against the Leopard 2A7 and intended to make a decision in late 2022.<ref>{{cite web |author=Per Erlien Dalløkken |date=12 April 2021 |title=Nye stridsvogner: Det blir tysk-koreansk duell i Norge |url=https://www.tu.no/artikler/nye-stridsvogner-det-blir-tysk-koreansk-duell-i-norge/509000 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220609075510/https://www.tu.no/artikler/nye-stridsvogner-det-blir-tysk-koreansk-duell-i-norge/509000 |archive-date=9 June 2022 |access-date=9 June 2022 |publisher=TU}}</ref>

In February 2023, the Norwegian government announced its decision to acquire 54 Leopard 2A7 main battle tanks from Germany,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://forsvaretsforum.no/innenriks-materiell-regjeringen/store-krigen-har-forsterket-argumentene-for-dette-tysk-norsk-nordiske-samarbeidet/308362|title=Støre: – Krigen har forsterket argumentene for dette tysk-norsk-nordiske samarbeidet|publisher=Forsvarets Forum|date=3 February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230204212512/https://forsvaretsforum.no/innenriks-materiell-regjeringen/store-krigen-har-forsterket-argumentene-for-dette-tysk-norsk-nordiske-samarbeidet/308362|archive-date=4 February 2023|access-date=4 February 2023|author=Andrea Rognstrand}}</ref> despite the Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency (FMA) twice recommending the K2 Black Panther from South Korea. The FMA's recommendation was based on a comprehensive assessment that found both tanks to be highly capable and to meet all operational requirements. However, the K2 was found to be "significantly lower" in price, weighed approximately 10 tons less, and offered a more traditional and less risky delivery schedule. The K2 also reportedly demonstrated superior mobility on snow and ice during winter trials.<ref name="k2no"/>

The government's final decision, however, was not based solely on technical and cost-efficiency. It was driven by broader strategic and security policy considerations. As explained by Prime Minister [[Jonas Gahr Støre]], purchasing German tanks ensures Norway has the same equipment as its Nordic neighbors—Sweden, Finland, and Denmark—thereby enhancing interoperability and collective defense within NATO. The decision also served to strengthen Norway's already close security and industrial ties with Germany, a key NATO partner and a major consumer of Norwegian natural gas. While a disappointment for Hyundai Rotem, the strong performance of the K2 in the Norwegian trials and the FMA's clear recommendation for it validated the tank's standing as a top-tier contender, likely boosting its reputation for future export opportunities to other NATO countries.<ref name="k2no">{{cite web|url=https://www.tu.no/artikler/forsvaret-anbefalte-koreanske-stridsvogner-likevel-valgte-regjeringen-a-kjope-tyske/528010?key=FmwLXVXl|title=Forsvarsmateriell anbefalte koreanske stridsvogner|date=16 March 2023}}</ref>

Leopard 2A7 tanks will take some time to arrive in Norway – the first are scheduled to be delivered between 2026 and 2031.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.technology.org/2023/09/10/norway-is-buying-new-leopard-tanks-they-will-have-a-unique-designation/#:~:text=Leopard%20tanks%20will%20take%20some,should%20be%20operational%20by%202031.|title=Norway is Buying New Leopard Tanks – They Will Have a Unique Designation|publisher=Technology.org|date=10 Sep 2023|access-date=10 Sep 2023|author=Technology.org}}</ref>

== Prototypes and variants ==
=== Prototypes ===
* '''XK2 MTR (Mobility Test Rig):''' Experimental vehicle for mobility tests, with main gun and electronic equipment removed from the turret. Only one was produced.
* '''XK2 FTR (Firepower Test Rig):''' Experimental vehicle for fire control, combat control, and low temperature operation tests. Like MTR, only one was produced for the experiment.
* '''XK2 PV (Pilot Vehicle):''' Experimental vehicle for the technical demonstration test of three XK2s, these vehicles were also called Pilot Vehicles and numbered PV1 through PV3. The main test objectives of these vehicles were endurance tests, developer tests, operator tests, and [[integrated logistics support]] tests.
** '''XK2:''' As the last prototype developed based on the '''XK2 PV''' released on 2 March 2007, the development was officially completed in September 2008 after the [[Operational acceptance testing|operational test]] of the [[Republic of Korea Army]].

=== Variants ===
* '''K2:''' Mass production variant with explosive reactive armor added to the sides of the turret and chassis. Deployed to the [[Republic of Korea Army]] starting 1 July 2014.
** '''K2 PIP (Product Improvement Program):''' The upgrade focuses on enhancing survivability and combat effectiveness by integrating a hard-kill active protection system (APS) to counter anti-tank missiles and drone threats, a 360-degree battlefield awareness system to improve crew situational awareness in urban and mountainous environments, and an AI-based Remote-Controlled Weapon Station (RCWS) for enhanced firepower. These improvements align with the evolving operational environment and the need for manned-unmanned collaborative combat capabilities.<ref>{{Cite web |last=박 |first=성균 |date=2023-11-19 |title=K2전차 성능개량 사업추진상황 |url=https://www.dapa.go.kr/dapa/na/ntt/selectNttInfo.do?bbsId=362&nttSn=46641&menuId=689 |access-date=2023-11-19 |website=[[Defense Acquisition Program Administration]] |language=Korean}}</ref>
* '''K2ME:''' Proposed licensed version of K2 for export to [[Middle East|middle eastern]] countries. It has an upgraded armor package and 7 road wheels, but unlike the K2, it lacks a Laser Warning Receiver (LWR) on the front of the turret.<ref name="K2M">{{cite web|url=http://kdtj.kipris.or.kr/kdtj/3020210019611%2CM001.pdf?method=fullText&applno=3020210019611,M001&pub_reg=R&ver=null&rights=DG|script-title=ko:지상 전투용 궤도차량|publisher=[[Korean Intellectual Property Office]]|date=20 June 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220827203338/http://kdtj.kipris.or.kr/kdtj/3020210019611,M001.pdf?method=fullText&applno=3020210019611,M001&pub_reg=R&ver=null&rights=DG|archive-date=27 August 2022|access-date=27 August 2022|author=[[Hyundai Rotem]]}}</ref>
* '''K2NO:''' Proposed licensed version of K2 for the [[Norwegian Armed Forces]] as a replacement for their aging fleet of [[Leopard 2#Leopard 2A4|Leopard 2A4]]. It is armed with a [[Trophy (countermeasure)|Trophy]] hard-kill APS, [[Composite armour|composite add-on armor]], a 12.7mm [[Remote controlled weapon station|RCWS]], and add-on [[Reactive armour|explosive reactive armor]]. In addition, preheating devices, battery heating packs, and electric air blow systems have been added to prevent the engine from turning off in Norway's cryogenic environment. The first few tanks were to be shipped from South Korea while the rest were to be built locally. The K2NO was competing against the [[Leopard 2#Leopard 2A7|Leopard 2A7]] in tank trials.{{citation needed|date=November 2025}} On February 3, 2023, the K2NO was rejected in favor of the Leopard 2A7.
*'''K2EX:''' Export variant presented at ADEX 2023. It incorporates an active protection system, called KAPS-2, a variant of the Trophy active protection system, a battlefield situational awareness device that provides 360° vision and a RCWS that incorporates an anti-drone gun. A notable feature of this variant is the incorporation of a modification that allows the ammunition to operate with information injection. This innovation allows the crew to control both the timing and shape of munition explosions, improving the adaptability of combat strategies.  The side armor of the turret and chassis was also improved.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Suciu |first=Peter |date=2024-06-20 |title=K2EX: The Best Tank on Earth (Not Made in USA) Is Getting Better |url=https://nationalinterest.org/blog/buzz/k2ex-best-tank-earth-not-made-usa-getting-better-211518 |access-date=2024-08-18 |website=The National Interest |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-11-21 |title=Hyundai Rotem Unveils K2EX Black Panther and N-WAV for Global Export - MilitaryLeak.COM |url=https://militaryleak.com/2023/11/21/hyundai-rotem-unveils-k2ex-black-panther-and-n-wav-for-global-export/?amp=1 |access-date=2024-08-18 |website=militaryleak.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-06-19 |title=Eurosatory 2024: Hyundai Rotem unveils upgraded K2 main battle tank |url=https://www.janes.com/osint-insights/defence-news/land/eurosatory-2024-hyundai-rotem-unveils-upgraded-k2-main-battle-tank |access-date=2024-08-18 |website=Default |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-06-18 |title=Eurosatory 2024: K2 z aktywną ochroną |url=https://defence24.pl/sily-zbrojne/eurosatory-2024-k2-z-aktywna-ochrona |access-date=2024-08-18 |website=defence24.pl |language=pl}}</ref>
* '''K2PL:''' Proposed licensed version of K2 for the [[Polish Armed Forces]] as a replacement for the aging fleet of [[PT-91]] tanks currently in service.<ref name="auto"/> The K2PL retains most of the K2's features, such as the CN08 120&nbsp;mm [[gun barrel]], bustle type autoloader, pulse-doppler radar and In-arm suspension unit (ISU), 6 road wheels, but it differs from the original version, among others: hard-kill [[Active protection system|APS]], anti-UAV [[electronic warfare]] system, [[Composite armour|composite add-on armor]], a 12.7mm [[Remote controlled weapon station|RCWS]], and add-on [[Reactive armour|explosive reactive armor]], additional armor of the turret and hull by adding detachable panels of layered armor, and in the case of the drive compartment, a mesh and bar armor, designed to protect against HEAT projectiles.{{Citation needed|date=September 2023}} Initially, the Polish side wanted the new tank to have an ammunition compartment separated from the crew compartment, but the design of the turret is not compatible with such a far-reaching change. After it turned out that this would require redesigning the hull and adding a seventh road wheel, the idea was abandoned. Under the framework agreement between [[Polska Grupa Zbrojeniowa|PGZ]] and Hyundai Rotem on the supply of K2 and K2PL, production of 820 K2PLs is scheduled to start in 2026 and will be divided between Poland and South Korea.<ref name="Dziennik Zbrojny" /><ref name="Polish Ministry of Defence" /><ref name="PGZ" /><ref name="Defence24" /><ref name="K2PL">{{cite web|url=http://kdtj.kipris.or.kr/kdtj/3020200045793%2CM001.pdf?method=fullText&applno=3020200045793,M001&pub_reg=R&ver=null&rights=DG|script-title=ko:지상 전투용 궤도차량|publisher=[[Korean Intellectual Property Office]]|date=5 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220827201945/http://kdtj.kipris.or.kr/kdtj/3020200045793,M001.pdf?method=fullText&applno=3020200045793,M001&pub_reg=R&ver=null&rights=DG|archive-date=27 August 2022|access-date=27 August 2022|author=[[Hyundai Rotem]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.militaeraktuell.at/koreanische-schwarze-panther-in-polen-gesichtet.html|title=KOREANISCHE "SCHWARZE PANTHER" IN POLEN|publisher=militaeraktuell|date=29 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331163329/https://www.militaeraktuell.at/koreanische-schwarze-panther-in-polen-gesichtet/|archive-date=31 March 2023|access-date=31 March 2023|author=militaeraktuell}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.defence24.pl/sily-zbrojne/borsuk-z-k2-abrams-z-ciezkim-bwp-czyli-odbudowa-wojsk-ladowych-gen-jablonski-kazdy-batalion-czolgow-jest-na-wage-zlota-wywiadz|title=Borsuk z K2, Abrams z ciężkim BWP czyli odbudowa Wojsk Lądowych. Gen. Jabłoński: "Każdy batalion czołgów jest na wagę złota" [WYWIAD]|publisher=Defence24|date=2 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230121110853/https://defence24.pl/sily-zbrojne/borsuk-z-k2-abrams-z-ciezkim-bwp-czyli-odbudowa-wojsk-ladowych-gen-jablonski-kazdy-batalion-czolgow-jest-na-wage-zlota-wywiad|archive-date=21 January 2023|access-date=21 January 2023|author=JĘDRZEJ GRAF}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/delfoarse/status/1621101698981953536|title=Hyundai Rotem K2 Tank road map for Polish and ROK Army|date=2 February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230919181400/https://twitter.com/delfoarse/status/1621101698981953536|archive-date=19 September 2023|access-date=19 September 2023|author=delfoarse}}</ref> In September 2025, Rafael Advanced Defense Systems and Hyundai Rotem announced an agreement to implement [[Trophy (countermeasure)|Trophy]] into the K2PL at MSPO 2025 Defense Exhibition.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg |first=Tzally |date=2025-09-05 |title=South Korea to integrate Trophy protective suite into K2 tanks |url=https://www.defensenews.com/global/asia-pacific/2025/09/05/south-korea-to-integrate-trophy-protective-suite-into-k2-tanks/ |access-date=2025-09-06 |website=Defense News |language=en}}</ref>

=== Support vehicles ===

=== Future operators ===
; {{flag|Peru}}
: On November 16, 2024, Hyundai Rotem announced  that it signed a comprehensive agreement with the Peruvian Army's Ordnance Factory (FAME S.A.C.) in Lima, Peru, for the supply of around 100 K2 tanks and other ground weapons. Hyundai Rotem President Lee Yong-bae and Jorge Zapata, the representative of the Peruvian Ordnance Factory, signed the 'Ground Equipment Cooperation Framework Agreement' in the presence of the heads of state from both Korea and Peru. This agreement aims to determine the total volume and scale of the K2 tank supply project before moving on to individual execution contracts, which will outline delivery schedules, detailed specifications, training, and maintenance conditions.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-18 |script-title=ko:현대로템, 페루와 지상무기 수출 총괄협약 체결 |url=https://www.hyundai.co.kr/news/CONT0000000000164731 |access-date=2024-11-18 |website=현대자동차그룹 뉴스룸 |language=ko}}</ref> The K2 Black Panther has been a strong contender for the Peruvian Army's "New MBT Acquisition Program," aimed at replacing its aging fleet of Soviet-era T-54/55 tanks. The K2's advanced features, particularly its hydropneumatic suspension system which allows it to operate effectively in diverse terrain, were seen as a major selling point for Peru's rugged mountainous interior. In November 2024, Hyundai Rotem and the Peruvian state-owned military production enterprise FAME S.A.C. signed a "General Cooperation Agreement," laying the groundwork for a potential purchase of 100 K2 tanks and future technology transfers for local production. The K2 was subsequently displayed at the SITDEF 2025 Defense Exhibition in Lima, further showcasing the tank's capabilities to Peruvian military officials.<ref name="moroco_peru_k2"/> In December 2025 ordered 54 tanks K2.<ref>{{Cite web |date = 2025-12-13 |title = Peru zamawia 195 czołgów i kto za 2 mld USD |url = https://www.altair.com.pl/peru-zamawia-195-czolgow-i-kto-za-2-mld-usd |access-date = 2024-10-07 |website = Altair |language = pl}}</ref>

=== Undisclosed operators ===
{{More citations needed section|date=July 2025}}
; {{flag|Saudi Arabia}}
: According to 2024 trade statistics, South Korea exported $115.73 million worth of "tanks" and armored vehicles to Saudi Arabia, which the value is increased by 7 times compared to 2023. A DAPA official told the details are confidential at Saudi Arabia’s request.<ref>{{Cite web |last=박혜원 |date=2025-01-15 |title=지난해 국산 전차 사우디 1억弗 깜짝 수출…중동으로 전선 넓히는 K-방산 |url=https://biz.heraldcorp.com/article/10390687 |access-date=2025-07-12 |website=헤럴드경제 |language=ko}}</ref> Saudi Arabia is reportedly only considering the K2 Black Panther among Korean tanks, and based on sales values, it's speculated that a single-digit number of prototype variants might be sold for testing before a larger purchase.

=== Potential operators ===
; {{flag|Armenia}}
: In October 2024, it was announced that Armenia might become an operator of the K2 Black Panther.<ref>{{Cite web |last = Kucharski |first = Bartłomiej |date = 2024-10-06 |title = Armenia potencjalnym użytkownikiem czołgów K2 |url=https://zbiam.pl/armenia-potencjalnym-uzytkownikiem-czolgow-k2/ |access-date = 2024-10-07 |website = Wydawnictwo militarne ZBIAM |language = pl}}</ref>
; {{flag|Egypt}}
: Egypt has revealed that it was seeking to procure the Black Panther as trade between the two nations has increased in recent years.<ref name="k2pip">{{Cite web |last=Carlin |date=27 February 2024 |title=K2 Black Panther: K2 PIP Upgrade Means This Monster Tank Is Scary Deadly |url=https://nationalinterest.org/blog/buzz/k2-black-panther-k2-pip-upgrade-means-monster-tank-scary-deadly-209733 |access-date=2024-02-27 |website=The National Interest}}</ref>
; {{flag|Iraq}}
: Expressed interest in purchasing an unknown amount of K2.<ref>{{Cite web |last = Świerkowski |first = Adam |date = 2026-01-28 |title = Korea sprzeda czołgi K2? Zastąpią T-72 produkowane w Polsce |url = https://defence24.pl/sily-zbrojne/korea-sprzeda-czolgi-k2-zastapia-t-72-produkowane-w-polsce |access-date = 2026-02-19 |website = Defence24 |language = pl}}</ref>
; {{flag|Morocco}}
: Morocco has shown significant interest in acquiring the K2 Black Panther as part of its ongoing military modernization efforts. In April 2025, Moroccan Minister of Industry and Trade Ryad Mezzour visited Seoul, where he reportedly discussed Rabat's intention to purchase the K2, along with the [[M-SAM]] air defense system and [[KSS-III]] submarines.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.military.africa/2026/02/morocco-evaluates-south-korean-k2-black-panther-main-battle-tank/|title=Morocco evaluates South Korean K2 Black Panther main battle tank - Military Africa|first1=Nzeadibe|last1=Ijeoma|first2=Military|last2=Africa}}</ref> The K2 is seen as a suitable complement to Morocco's existing fleet of American-made M1A2 Abrams tanks. The potential acquisition of advanced South Korean military hardware highlights the deepening defense and economic ties between the two nations, with a previous deal for double-decker trains also being finalized between Morocco and Hyundai Rotem.<ref name="moroco_peru_k2">{{Cite web |last=Suciu |first=Peter |date=2025-04-24 |title=Why Morocco and Peru Want to Buy South Korea's K2 Black |url=https://nationalinterest.org/blog/buzz/why-morocco-and-peru-want-to-buy-south-koreas-k2-black-panther-tank |website=The National Interest |language=en}}</ref>
; {{flag|Romania}}
: Romania is interested in purchasing additional tanks to replace its existing fleet of [[TR-85|TR-85-800]] and [[TR-85|TR-85M1]]. The target mentioned in the local media is of 300 new tanks on top of the 54 [[M1A2 Abrams]] already ordered.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Atlamazoglou |first=Constantine |date=2023-09-27 |title=As Russia's war in Ukraine drags on, Kyiv's neighbors are loading up on new high-tech military gear |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/poland-romania-buying-military-weapons-amid-russia-ukraine-war-2023-9 |access-date=2023-09-27 |website=Business Insider |language=en}}</ref> According to Hyundai Rotem, the target is closer to 500 units.<ref name="hk240405">{{Cite web |last=Bae |first=Changhak |date=2024-04-05 |script-title=ko:[단독] 현대로템 K2, 내달 루마니아서 실사격...최종 테스트 |url=https://www.hankyung.com/article/2024040515515 |access-date=2024-04-05 |website=[[The Korea Economic Daily]] |language=ko}}</ref>
: The Romanian armed forces have approached Germany and South Korea and their defence industry for that programme. The K2 Black Panther tank underwent live-fire testing at the Smârdan training range in Romania in May 2024.<ref>{{cite web |date=16 May 2024 |title=Tancul K-2 "Black Panther", aflat pe lista de dorinţe a Ministerului Apărării, este testat în România la poligonul din Smârdan (Foto) |url=https://www.defenseromania.ro/aflat-pe-lista-de-dorinte-a-ministerului-apararii-este-testat-in-romania-la-poligonul-din-smardan_628321.html |work=DefenseRomania |language=ro}}</ref>

=== Failed bids ===
; {{flag|Norway}}
: Norway put the K2 in competition against the [[Leopard 2|Leopard 2A7V]] which was selected by the Norwegian Army in 2023, and later on the [[Leopard 2#Leopard 2A8 NOR|Leopard 2A8]] was ordered.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Norway's Leopard 2 tanks will be new 2A8 variant with active protection system |publisher=Shephard |url=https://www.shephardmedia.com/news/landwarfareintl/configuration-is-finalised-for-norways-leopard-2a8-tank-order/ |access-date=2024-10-07 |language=en}}</ref>
; {{flag|Slovakia}}
: In 2021, Slovakia discussed a potential K2 buy at the ministerial level.<ref>{{Cite web |last=ROBLIN |first=SÉBASTIEN |date=2023-03-31 |title=Can Germany's big cats resist South Korea's Black Panther invasion? |url=https://breakingdefense.com/2023/03/can-germanys-big-cats-resist-south-koreas-black-panther-invasion/ |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=Breaking Defense |language=en}}</ref> In February 2025, Slovak and Polish Defence Ministers Robert Kalinak and Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz signed an agreement on the intention to strengthen cooperation in the arms industry. The Polish minister mentioned Slovakia's interest in Korean K2 tanks, which the Poles will produce in a modified version on their territory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Antalik |first=Marek |date=2025-02-24 |title=Poland and Slovakia Sign Agreement on Intention to Boost Defence Cooperation |url=https://newsnow.tasr.sk/poland-and-slovakia-sign-agreement-on-intention-to-boost-defence-cooperation/ |access-date=2025-02-24 |website=News Now |language=en}}</ref> Due to changes in the plan and the desire to reduce costs, the decision was made to purchase light tanks of Swedish or Turkish production instead of main battle tanks.<ref>{{Cite web |last = Kucharski |first = Bartłomiej |date = 2025-09-26 |title = Słowacja rezygnuje z K2PL na rzecz czołgu średniego? [Wideo] |url = https://zbiam.pl/slowacja-rezygnuje-z-k2pl-na-rzecz-czolgu-sredniego/ |access-date = 2026-02-19 |website = Zbiam |language = pl}}</ref>
